units.note: 大月氏五翕侯之一，1 世纪前半丘就却统一五部，自立为王，南侵罽宾、高附，阎膏珍时兼有天竺西北。90 年遣副王谢率七万众越葱岭攻班超，粮尽而退。
units.notee: One of the five Yuezhi yabghus. In the first half of the 1st century Kujula Kadphises united the five and made himself king, invading Jibin and Gaofu; under Vima Taktu (Yangaozhen) the Kushans also held north-western India. In AD 90 the viceroy Xie led 70,000 men over the Pamirs against Ban Chao but withdrew when supplies ran out.

units.note: 塔里木盆地周缘的城郭诸国，《汉书》称三十六国，后分至五十余国。汉初役属匈奴，匈奴设僮仆都尉；前60 年匈奴日逐王降汉，郑吉为西域都护，诸国内属。新莽时绝；东汉 74、91 年两度复置都护，107 年又罢，123 年后以西域长史领之。
units.notee: The walled oasis states around the Tarim Basin, thirty-six according to the Han shu and later over fifty. In early Han they were subject to the Xiongnu, who kept a Commandant of Slaves there; in 60 BC the Xiongnu Rizhu king surrendered to Han, Zheng Ji became Protector-General and the states submitted. They were lost under Wang Mang; the Eastern Han restored the Protector-General in 74 and 91, abolished the post again in 107 and from 123 governed through a Chief Clerk of the Western Regions.

units.note: 塔里木盆地北缘的龟兹、姑墨、温宿、尉头、焉耆、尉犁诸国。龟兹王建为匈奴所立，「倚恃虏威，据有北道」；75 年焉耆、龟兹攻没都护陈睦。91 年龟兹、姑墨、温宿降班超，94 年班超斩焉耆王广，北道始平。图上 74、76、89 年单独画出，画作役属北匈奴，其余年份并入西域诸国。
units.notee: Kucha, Gumo, Wensu, Weitou, Karasahr and Yuli on the northern rim of the Tarim Basin. Jian, king of Kucha, had been set up by the Xiongnu and, 'relying on the barbarians' power, held the northern route'; in 75 Karasahr and Kucha attacked and killed the Protector-General Chen Mu. Kucha, Gumo and Wensu submitted to Ban Chao in 91, and in 94 Ban Chao beheaded Guang, king of Karasahr, and the northern route was finally pacified. The map draws them separately in 74, 76 and 89, as subject to the Northern Xiongnu; in other years they are part of the States of the Western Regions.

units.note: 班超经营西域时据为根本的南道诸国。73 年班超以三十六人使鄯善、于阗，皆降；74 年至疏勒，执龟兹所立的疏勒王兜题，立故王兄子忠。76 年罢都护，班超奉诏东归，于阗王侯抱马脚号泣，超遂还疏勒，与疏勒、于阗坚守，以其兵攻姑墨（78）、破莎车（87），91 年为西域都护。图上 73、76、89 年单独画出，画作内属于汉（斜线）。
units.notee: The southern-route states that were Ban Chao's base in the Western Regions. In 73 he went with thirty-six men to Shanshan and Khotan, and both submitted; in 74 he reached Kashgar, seized Douti, the king Kucha had imposed there, and set up Zhong, a nephew of the former king. When the Protectorate was abandoned in 76 Ban Chao was ordered home, but at Khotan the king and nobles clung weeping to his horse's legs, and he went back to Kashgar and held on there and in Khotan, using their troops against Gumo (78) and Yarkand (87); in 91 he became Protector-General. The map draws them separately in 73, 76 and 89, as submitting to Han (hatched).

units.note: 河湟与青海一带的部族，种落繁多，先零、烧当最强。汉置护羌校尉，屡有反叛；东汉 107—118、140—145、159—169 年羌乱迭起，凉州残破。
units.notee: Peoples of the Yellow River and Huangshui valleys (Hehuang) and Qinghai, divided into many tribes of which the Xianlian and Shaodang were the strongest. Han appointed a Protector of the Qiang, but revolts were frequent; under the Eastern Han the Qiang wars of 107–118, 140–145 and 159–169 left Liang Province in ruins.

units.note: 秦南海尉赵佗，秦亡后绝道自守，击并桂林、象郡，前204 年自立为南越武王，都番禺；前196 年受汉封，吕后时称帝，又攻并瓯雒。前112 年丞相吕嘉反汉，次年汉灭南越，置九郡。
units.notee: Zhao Tuo, the Qin commandant of Nanhai, cut the roads after Qin fell and annexed Guilin and Xiang commanderies, making himself King Wu of Nanyue in 204 BC with his capital at Panyu. He accepted a Han title in 196 BC, proclaimed himself emperor under Empress Lü and annexed Âu Lạc. In 112 BC the chancellor Lü Jia rebelled against Han, and the next year Han destroyed Nanyue and set up nine commanderies.

units.note: 红河三角洲的安阳王之国（越南史称瓯雒国），前180 年前后为南越所并，置交趾、九真二郡守之。
units.notee: The kingdom of King An Dương in the Red River delta, absorbed by Nanyue around 180 BC and governed as the commanderies of Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen.

units.note: 越王勾践之后无诸，秦时废为君长；佐汉灭楚，前202 年封闽越王，都东冶。前138 年围东瓯，前135 年攻南越，屡与汉为敌；前110 年汉灭之，徙其民于江淮。
units.notee: Wuzhu, a descendant of King Goujian of Yue, was reduced to a chieftain under Qin; he helped Han destroy Chu and was made king of Minyue at Dongye in 202 BC. Minyue besieged Dong'ou in 138 BC and attacked Nanyue in 135 BC, repeatedly defying Han; Han destroyed it in 110 BC and moved its people to the Yangzi–Huai region.

units.note: 无诸同族的摇，佐汉有功，前192 年封东海王，都东瓯（今温州），俗称东瓯王。前138 年为闽越所围，汉救之，东瓯举国四万余人内徙江淮。
units.notee: Yao, a kinsman of Wuzhu, was rewarded for helping Han and made king of Donghai at Dong'ou (modern Wenzhou) in 192 BC, commonly called the king of Dong'ou. Besieged by Minyue in 138 BC and relieved by Han, the whole kingdom of over forty thousand people moved inland to the Yangzi–Huai region.

units.note: 西南夷中最大的君长国，在今贵州西部。前135 年唐蒙通夜郎，置犍为郡；前111 年夜郎王入朝受印，以其地为牂柯郡。
units.notee: The largest of the southwestern chiefdoms, in western Guizhou. Tang Meng opened the route to Yelang in 135 BC and Qianwei Commandery was set up; in 111 BC the king of Yelang came to court and received a seal, and his land became Zangke Commandery.

units.note: 滇池一带的君长国，战国时楚将庄蹻入滇称王。前109 年汉兵临滇，滇王举国降，赐滇王之印，置益州郡。
units.notee: A chiefdom around Lake Dian, where the Chu general Zhuang Qiao had made himself king in the Warring States period. When Han troops arrived in 109 BC the king of Dian surrendered his whole kingdom, received the seal of King of Dian, and Yizhou Commandery was set up.

units.note: 安宁河谷的君长国，与筰都并称邛筰。前111 年置越嶲郡。
units.notee: A chiefdom of the Anning valley, named together with Zuodu as Qiong–Zuo. Yuexi Commandery was set up there in 111 BC.

units.note: 澜沧江以西的部族国家，东汉 51 年一部内附，69 年哀牢王柳貌率众内属，置永昌郡，汉地西至伊洛瓦底江。
units.notee: A tribal state west of the Mekong. Part of it submitted to Han in AD 51, and in 69 King Liumao of Ailao brought his people in; Yongchang Commandery was set up, carrying Han territory west to the Irrawaddy.

units.note: 巴蜀以南、以西的众多部族：冉駹、筰都、白马、昆明、嶲、靡莫等，大者为君长国，小者随畜迁徙。武帝时陆续置郡，昆明诸部屡阻通身毒之道。
units.notee: The many peoples south and west of Ba and Shu — the Ranmang, Zuodu, Baima, Kunming, Xi, Mimo and others — some organised as chiefdoms, others herders on the move. Emperor Wu brought them under commanderies one by one, though the Kunming tribes repeatedly blocked the route to India.

units.note: 秦汉之际为箕氏朝鲜（王否、王准）。前194 年燕人卫满率众东渡浿水，逐准王，都王险城，役属真番、临屯，是为卫氏朝鲜。前109 年汉遣杨仆、荀彘水陆并进，次年王险城降，置乐浪、真番、临屯、玄菟四郡。
units.notee: At the end of Qin, Joseon was ruled by the Gija line (kings Bu and Jun). In 194 BC Wiman of Yan crossed the Pae River with his followers, drove out King Jun and ruled from Wangxian, making Zhenfan and Lintun his dependencies: this was Wiman Joseon. Han sent Yang Pu and Xun Zhi by sea and land in 109 BC; Wangxian surrendered the next year and the four commanderies of Lelang, Zhenfan, Lintun and Xuantu were set up.

units.note: 东北亚的濊、貊诸部，分布于鸭绿江、浑江流域至朝鲜半岛东部。前128 年濊君南闾降汉，置苍海郡，二年而罢。
units.notee: The Ye and Maek peoples of north-east Asia, from the Yalu and Hun valleys to the east of the Korean peninsula. In 128 BC the Ye chief Namnyeo submitted to Han and Canghai Commandery was set up, abolished two years later.

units.note: 朝鲜半岛东北的部族，汉初属卫氏朝鲜，汉武帝以后属玄菟、乐浪；30 年罢东部都尉后自立，旋臣属高句丽。
units.notee: A people of the north-east of the Korean peninsula, subject first to Wiman Joseon and after Emperor Wu to Xuantu and Lelang; after the Eastern Commandant was abolished in AD 30 they became independent but were soon subject to Goguryeo.

units.note: 松嫩平原的农牧之国，都今吉林市一带，与汉亲善，东汉时屡遣使朝贡。
units.notee: A farming and herding state of the Songnen plain with its capital near modern Jilin City, friendly to Han; it sent envoys to the Eastern Han court many times.

units.note: 前37 年朱蒙于卒本（今桓仁）立国，3 年迁都国内城（今集安）。王莽时改称下句丽；东汉时屡寇辽东、玄菟。
units.notee: Founded at Jolbon (Huanren) by Jumong in 37 BC, Goguryeo moved its capital to Gungnae (Ji'an) in AD 3. Wang Mang renamed it Xia-Gouli; under the Eastern Han it repeatedly raided Liaodong and Xuantu.

units.note: 朝鲜半岛南部诸部，汉初称辰国，准王南奔后称韩王；东汉时分为马韩、辰韩、弁韩，共七十八国，以马韩为大。
units.notee: The peoples of the southern Korean peninsula, called Jin in early Han; King Jun, fleeing south, styled himself King of Han (韓) there. Under the Eastern Han they formed the Mahan, Jinhan and Byeonhan — seventy-eight small states, Mahan the largest.

units.note: 灭东周、取成皋荥阳后所置，以河、洛、伊三川得名。治洛阳。
units.notee: Set up after the destruction of East Zhou and the capture of Chenggao and Xingyang; named after the three rivers He, Luo and Yi. Seat at Luoyang.

units.note: 治怀。
units.notee: Seat at Huai.

units.note: 治安邑。
units.notee: Seat at Anyi.

units.note: 京畿之地，不设郡，由内史直辖。治咸阳。
units.notee: The metropolitan region, not organised as a commandery but administered directly by the Neishi. Seat at Xianyang.

units.note: 治濮阳。
units.notee: Seat at Puyang.

units.note: 治阳翟。
units.notee: Seat at Yangdi.

units.note: 取楚陈地所置。《史记》作“楚郡”，后世或称陈郡。治陈。
units.notee: Set up from Chu's Chen region. Called "Chu Commandery" in the Shiji, and sometimes Chen Commandery later. Seat at Chen.

units.note: 灭魏后以其东部所置。治睢阳。
units.notee: Set up from the eastern part of Wei after its destruction. Seat at Suiyang.

units.note: 取楚淮北所置。岳麓书院秦简作“四川”，《汉书·地理志》《水经注》作“泗水郡”。刘邦即此郡沛县人。治相。
units.notee: Set up from Chu's lands north of the Huai. Written 四川 (Sichuan) in the Yuelu Academy Qin slips and 泗水 (Sishui) in the Hanshu treatise on geography and the Shuijing zhu. Liu Bang came from Pei County in this commandery. Seat at Xiang.

units.note: 取鲁、薛故地所置。治鲁。
units.notee: Set up from the former lands of Lu and Xue. Seat at Lu.

units.note: 治寿春。
units.notee: Seat at Shouchun.

units.note: 破赵所置。治邯郸。
units.notee: Set up after Zhao was crushed. Seat at Handan.

units.note: 治巨鹿。
units.notee: Seat at Julu.

units.note: 以赵中山故地所置，岳麓书院秦简可证。汉避文帝讳改称常山。治东垣。
units.notee: Set up from the former Zhongshan lands of Zhao, attested in the Yuelu Academy Qin slips. Renamed Changshan under the Han to avoid the personal name of Emperor Wen. Seat at Dongyuan.

units.note: 治清阳。
units.notee: Seat at Qingyang.

units.note: 破燕都蓟后所置（一说秦无广阳郡）。治蓟。
units.notee: Set up after the Yan capital Ji was taken (one view: Qin had no Guangyang Commandery). Seat at Ji.

units.note: 后晓荣《秦代政区地理》所考（一说）。治博阳。
units.notee: Identified by Hou Xiaorong in Qindai zhengqu dili (one view). Seat at Boyang.

units.note: 秦封泥见“济北太守”，一般认为统一后析置。治庐。
units.notee: A Qin clay sealing reads "governor of Jibei"; generally thought to have been split off after unification. Seat at Lu.

units.note: 治郯。
units.notee: Seat at Tan.

units.note: 治吴。
units.notee: Seat at Wu.

units.note: 王国维《秦郡考》所列，秦封泥见“城阳”（一说）。治莒。
units.notee: Listed in Wang Guowei's Qin jun kao; a Qin clay sealing reads "Chengyang" (one view). Seat at Ju.

units.note: 灭齐所置。秦封泥作“临菑”，《汉书·地理志》作“齐郡”。治临菑。
units.notee: Set up after the destruction of Qi. Written 临菑 (Linzi) on Qin clay sealings and called Qi Commandery in the Hanshu treatise on geography. Seat at Linzi.

units.note: 秦封泥见“即墨太守”，即胶东之地。治即墨。
units.notee: A Qin clay sealing reads "governor of Jimo": the Jiaodong region. Seat at Jimo.

units.note: 治宛。
units.notee: Seat at Wan.

units.note: 治江陵。
units.notee: Seat at Jiangling.

units.note: 岳麓书院秦简可证，一般认为统一后析置。治邾。
units.notee: Attested in the Yuelu Academy Qin slips; generally thought to have been split off after unification. Seat at Zhu.

units.note: 治广信。
units.notee: Seat at Guangxin.

units.note: 里耶秦简、岳麓书院秦简所见郡名，迁陵县即隶洞庭郡。《史记》所载前277 所置“黔中郡”是否存在、与洞庭郡是何关系，学界有争议。治临沅（一说）。
units.notee: A commandery name attested in the Liye and Yuelu Academy Qin slips; Qianling County belonged to Dongting Commandery. Whether the Qianzhong Commandery the Shiji records as set up in 277 BC existed, and how it related to Dongting, is disputed among scholars. Seat at Linyuan (one view).

units.note: 定楚江南所置。治临湘。
units.notee: Set up after Chu's lands south of the Yangtze were pacified. Seat at Linxiang.

units.note: 治西城。
units.notee: Seat at Xicheng.

units.note: 平岭南所置。治布山。
units.notee: Set up after Lingnan was pacified. Seat at Bushan.

units.note: 治番禺。
units.notee: Seat at Panyu.

units.note: 废闽越王为君长，以其地为闽中郡，实为羁縻。治东冶。
units.notee: The king of Minyue was reduced to a chieftain and his land made Minzhong Commandery, in practice a loose-rein arrangement. Seat at Dongye.

units.note: 治江州。
units.notee: Seat at Jiangzhou.

units.note: 治成都。
units.notee: Seat at Chengdu.

units.note: 治狄道。
units.notee: Seat at Didao.

units.note: 治马领。
units.notee: Seat at Maling.

units.note: 治长子。
units.notee: Seat at Zhangzi.

units.note: 治晋阳。
units.notee: Seat at Jinyang.

units.note: 治肤施。
units.notee: Seat at Fushi.

units.note: 取河南地后所置，直道北端。治九原。
units.notee: Set up after Henandi was taken; the northern end of the Straight Road. Seat at Jiuyuan.

units.note: 治云中。
units.notee: Seat at Yunzhong.

units.note: 治善无。
units.notee: Seat at Shanwu.

units.note: 治代。
units.notee: Seat at Dai.

units.note: 治沮阳。
units.notee: Seat at Juyang.

units.note: 治渔阳。
units.notee: Seat at Yuyang.

units.note: 治平刚。
units.notee: Seat at Pinggang.

units.note: 治且虑。
units.notee: Seat at Julü.

units.note: 治襄平。
units.notee: Seat at Xiangping.

units.note: 平岭南所置。辖境一说南及今越南中北部，一说只在今广西西南部。治临尘。
units.notee: Set up after Lingnan was pacified. By one view it extended south into north-central Vietnam; by another it lay only in what is now SW Guangxi. Seat at Linchen.

units.note: 治东武。
units.notee: Seat at Dongwu.

units.note: 汉初赵国领邯郸、巨鹿、常山、清河诸郡，张耳、张敖后为刘如意、刘友等；七国之乱后国除，前152 年复置，地渐小。
units.notee: Early Han Zhao held Handan, Julu, Changshan and Qinghe under Zhang Er and Zhang Ao and then Liu Ruyi, Liu You and others; abolished after the Rebellion of the Seven States, it was restored in 152 BC on a smaller scale.

units.note: 汉初齐国（刘肥）领七十余城，为诸侯王之最大者；后屡被分割，前164 年分为六国，前127 年齐王刘次昌自杀国除。
units.notee: The early Han kingdom of Qi under Liu Fei held more than seventy towns, the largest of all; it was repeatedly divided, into six kingdoms in 164 BC, and abolished when its king Liu Cichang killed himself in 127 BC.

units.note: 韩王信（韩襄王孙）随汉定韩地，前205 年立为韩王，都阳翟；前201 年徙太原，都马邑，同年降匈奴。
units.notee: Han Xin, a grandson of King Xiang of Han (韓) and not the general of the same name, won back the Han (韓) lands for Liu Bang and was made king of Han (韓) at Yangdi in 205 BC; moved to Taiyuan with his capital at Mayi in 201 BC, he went over to the Xiongnu the same year.

units.note: 英布为淮南王，前196 年反，次年兵败被杀，改封刘长；刘长前174 年谋反废死。前164 年三分淮南，刘安为淮南王，前122 年谋反国除。
units.notee: Ying Bu was king of Huainan until his revolt in 196 BC (he was killed the following year), then Liu Chang, who was deposed for plotting in 174 BC. In 164 BC Huainan was split in three, Liu An becoming king of Huainan; he was found plotting in 122 BC and the kingdom was abolished.

units.note: 汉初燕国领广阳、上谷至辽东诸郡；臧荼、卢绾后为刘建、刘泽等，前128 年国除，前117 年刘旦复封，前80 年谋反国除。
units.notee: Early Han Yan held the commanderies from Guangyang and Shanggu to Liaodong under Zang Tu and Lu Wan and then Liu Jian, Liu Ze and others; abolished in 128 BC, it was refounded for Liu Dan in 117 BC and abolished again after his plot of 80 BC.

units.note: 彭越为梁王，都定陶；前196 年被诛，改封刘恢。文帝子梁孝王刘武领四十余城，七国之乱中坚守睢阳；前144 年分梁为五国。
units.notee: Peng Yue was king of Liang at Dingtao until executed in 196 BC; Liu Hui replaced him. Liu Wu, Emperor Wen's son, held over forty towns as King Xiao of Liang and held Suiyang during the Rebellion of the Seven States; in 144 BC Liang was split into five.

units.note: 汉初韩信为楚王，前201 年废，分淮西为楚国（刘交，都彭城）、淮东为荆国。前154 年被削东海郡，楚王遂参与七国之乱；乱后只领彭城一郡之地。
units.notee: Han Xin was king of Chu in early Han until deposed in 201 BC; west of the Huai became Chu under Liu Jiao (capital Pengcheng) and east of it Jing. Stripped of Donghai in 154 BC, its king joined the Rebellion of the Seven States; afterwards it held only the area of Pengcheng.

units.note: 吴芮为长沙王，是汉初唯一存续的异姓王国，传五世至前157 年无后国除；前155 年景帝封子刘发为长沙王。
units.notee: Wu Rui's Changsha was the only kingdom under a king outside the imperial Liu clan to survive early Han, lasting five generations until it died out in 157 BC; in 155 BC Emperor Jing made his son Liu Fa king of Changsha.

units.note: 前201 年以淮东五十余城封刘贾为荆王，都吴；前196 年刘贾为英布所杀，国除，前195 年改封刘濞为吴王。
units.notee: Liu Jia was made king of Jing in 201 BC with over fifty towns east of the Huai, ruling from Wu; he was killed by Ying Bu in 196 BC and the kingdom was refounded as Wu under Liu Bi in 195 BC.

units.note: 汉初以颍川、淮阳封刘友，后屡废屡置；宣帝时以陈为淮阳国。
units.notee: First given to Liu You with Yingchuan and Huaiyang in early Han, the kingdom was repeatedly abolished and restored; under Emperor Xuan it was re-established around Chen.

units.note: 刘濞为吴王，都广陵，煮海为盐、即山铸钱，富甲诸侯；前154 年首倡七国之乱，兵败国除。
units.notee: Liu Bi, king of Wu, ruled from Guangling, boiling sea water for salt and minting coin from the copper of its hills, the richest of the kings; he led the Rebellion of the Seven States in 154 BC and his kingdom was abolished after his defeat.

units.note: 前196 年封刘恒为代王，都中都，后为文帝；领代、雁门、太原等郡，前114 年代王刘义徙清河，代国除。
units.notee: Liu Heng, later Emperor Wen, was made king of Dai in 196 BC with his capital at Zhongdu; Dai held Dai, Yanmen and Taiyuan commanderies until its king Liu Yi was moved to Qinghe in 114 BC and the kingdom was abolished.

units.note: 吕后割齐之琅邪封刘泽为琅邪王；前179 年刘泽徙燕，地还齐。
units.notee: Empress Lü carved Langya out of Qi for Liu Ze; in 179 BC he was moved to Yan and the land went back to Qi.

units.note: 治雒阳。
units.notee: Seat at Luoyang.

units.note: 治弘农。
units.notee: Seat at Hongnong.

units.note: 治长安。
units.notee: Seat at Chang'an.

units.note: 治高陵。
units.notee: Seat at Gaoling.

units.note: 治槐里。
units.notee: Seat at Huaili.

units.note: 治平舆。
units.notee: Seat at Pingyu.

units.note: 治鲁。
units.notee: Seat at Lu.

units.note: 治邺。
units.notee: Seat at Ye.

units.note: 治卢奴。
units.notee: Seat at Lunu.

units.note: 治信都。
units.notee: Seat at Xindu.

units.note: 治乐成。
units.notee: Seat at Lecheng.

units.note: 治浮阳。
units.notee: Seat at Fuyang.

units.note: 前164 年齐分出的王国之一，领泰山以北之地。
units.notee: One of the kingdoms carved out of Qi in 164 BC, holding the land north of Mount Tai.

units.note: 前164 年齐分出的王国之一，济南王刘辟光参与七国之乱，国除为郡。
units.notee: One of the kingdoms carved out of Qi in 164 BC; its king Liu Piguang joined the Rebellion of the Seven States and it became a commandery.

units.note: 治平原。
units.notee: Seat at Pingyuan.

units.note: 治千乘。
units.notee: Seat at Qiancheng.

units.note: 前164 年齐分出的王国，七国之乱中胶西王刘卬为首谋之一，兵败自杀；后封刘端，前108 年国除。
units.notee: Carved out of Qi in 164 BC; its king Liu Ang was among the leaders of the Rebellion of the Seven States and killed himself after defeat; Liu Duan then held it until it was abolished in 108 BC.

units.note: 治掖。
units.notee: Seat at Ye.

units.note: 前164 年淮南三分之一，刘勃、刘赐先后为王；前122 年刘赐谋反国除。
units.notee: One of the three parts of Huainan from 164 BC, ruled by Liu Bo and then Liu Ci; abolished when Liu Ci was found plotting in 122 BC.

units.note: 前164 年淮南三分之一，刘赐为王，前153 年徙衡山，国除为郡。
units.notee: One of the three parts of Huainan from 164 BC under Liu Ci, who was moved to Hengshan in 153 BC, the kingdom becoming a commandery.

units.note: 治梓潼。
units.notee: Seat at Zitong.

units.note: 治僰道。
units.notee: Seat at Bodao.

units.note: 治平襄。

e.note: In 69, while taming the Yellow River, Wang Jing also restored the Bian Canal, which ran east from Xingyang past Junyi and Suiyang to join the Si at Pengcheng. It was the main waterway from Luoyang to Xu and Yang provinces; Guandu lay on its upper course.

items.note: 战国魏惠王时（前360 年起）开凿，自荥阳引河水东经大梁，南下至陈入颍，沟通河、淮；《汉书·地理志》称狼汤渠，北魏《水经注》作蒗荡渠。前203 年楚汉相持日久，项羽与汉约「中分天下，割鸿沟以西者为汉，鸿沟而东者为楚」，归还太公、吕后引兵东归；汉王用张良、陈平之计背约追击，次年垓下灭楚。后世象棋盘上的「楚河汉界」一般认为即由此而来。走向与战国卷相同。

e.mod: along the Jialu and Shaying rivers
e.note: Dug from 360 BC under King Hui of Wei, it drew water from the Yellow River at Xingyang, ran east past Daliang and then south to Chen, where it joined the Ying, linking the Yellow River and the Huai. The treatise on geography in the Hanshu calls it the Langtang Canal, and the Northern Wei Commentary on the Water Classic the Langdang Canal. In 203 BC, after a long stand-off between Chu and Han, Xiang Yu agreed with Han to 'divide the realm in two, the land west of the Honggou to Han and the land east of it to Chu', handed back the king of Han's father and wife and marched his army east; on the advice of Zhang Liang and Chen Ping the king of Han broke the agreement and pursued him, destroying Chu at Gaixia the next year. The 'Chu river, Han border' across the middle of the Chinese chessboard is generally thought to come from this. Drawn along the same course as in the Warring States volume.

items.note: 春秋吴王夫差所开，沟通江淮。

e.note: Dug by Fuchai, King of Wu, in the Spring and Autumn period to link the Yangtze and the Huai.

items.note: 秦汉已有自吴通京口的水道，孙吴时为建业与吴会之间的漕路。

e.note: A waterway from Wu to Jingkou already existed in the Qin and Han; under Sun Wu it was the grain route between Jianye and Wu and Kuaiji.

items.note: 西汉武帝时所开，自长安引渭水东至华阴。

e.note: Dug under Emperor Wu of the Western Han, it led water from the Wei River east from Chang'an to Huayin.

items.note: 秦所开，沟通湘、漓二水。

e.note: Dug under the Qin to link the Xiang and Li rivers.

items.note: 关中与汉中的天然屏障，其间有子午、傥骆、褒斜、陈仓诸道。诸葛亮五次北伐都要翻越秦岭，粮运艰难是蜀汉北伐最大的掣肘。

e.note: The natural barrier between Guanzhong and Hanzhong, crossed by the Ziwu, Tangluo, Baoye and Chencang roads. All five of Zhuge Liang's northern campaigns had to cross the Qinling, and the difficulty of moving grain over them was the greatest constraint on Shu Han's campaigns.

items.note: 汉中与巴蜀之间的屏障，米仓道、金牛道穿越其间。

e.note: The barrier between Hanzhong and Ba–Shu, crossed by the Micang and Jinniu roads.

items.note: 河北与并州的分界。黄巾余部黑山军张燕盘踞其中，众号百万。

e.note: The divide between Hebei and Bing Province. Zhang Yan's Black Mountain army, a Yellow Turban remnant said to number a million, was based in these mountains.

items.note: 漠南的屏障，匈奴依以为苑囿。前127 年卫青收河南地，复缮秦塞；侯应称匈奴失阴山之后，「过之未尝不哭也」。

e.note: The barrier south of the Gobi, which the Xiongnu used as their hunting park. After Wei Qing recovered the Ordos in 127 BC the Qin frontier was repaired; Hou Ying said that after losing the Yin Mountains the Xiongnu 'never passed them without weeping'.

items.note: 关中与陇右的分界，陇关、萧关扼其要道。

e.note: The divide between Guanzhong and Longyou, its main routes guarded by the Long and Xiao passes.

items.note: 颜师古注：「匈奴谓天为祁连。」前121 年夏霍去病逾居延至祁连山，大破匈奴。匈奴失祁连、焉支二山，歌曰「亡我祁连山，使我六畜不蕃息」。

e.note: Yan Shigu notes that 'the Xiongnu call Heaven qilian'. In the summer of 121 BC Huo Qubing passed Juyan and reached the Qilian Mountains, crushing the Xiongnu. Having lost the Qilian and Yanzhi mountains, the Xiongnu sang, 'We have lost our Qilian Mountains, and our herds no longer thrive.'

items.note: 91 年耿夔、任尚于此大破北单于。

e.note: In 91 Geng Kui and Ren Shang routed the Northern Chanyu here.

items.note: 蒙古高原西部的主脉。汉代的燕然山一般认为是其东南的余脉：2017 年在蒙古国中戈壁省德勒格尔杭爱找到了《封燕然山铭》摩崖（见「燕然山」）。

e.note: The main range of the western Mongolian plateau. The Han dynasty's Mount Yanran is generally taken to be an outlier to its south-east: in 2017 the cliff inscription for the feng sacrifice on Mount Yanran was found at Delgerkhangai in Dundgovi Province, Mongolia (see Mount Yanran).

items.note: 南阳盆地北缘，鲁阳、叶县扼其东口。

e.note: The northern rim of the Nanyang Basin, its eastern outlets guarded by Luyang and She County.

items.note: 魏吴江淮之间的屏障，魏弋阳与吴蕲春隔山相望。

e.note: The barrier between Wei and Wu in the Jiang–Huai region; Wei's Yiyang and Wu's Qichun faced each other across the mountains.

items.note: 东汉 69 年哀牢国内附，以其地置永昌郡。

e.note: In 69 the Ailao kingdom submitted to the Eastern Han, which made its lands into Yongchang Commandery.

items.note: 洛阳北面的黄土岭，东汉帝陵不少在其上，有“生在苏杭，葬在北邙”之说；189 年董卓于北邙迎回少帝。

e.note: The loess ridge north of Luoyang, where many of the Eastern Han emperors were buried; there is a saying "Be born in Suzhou or Hangzhou, be buried at Beimang". In 189 Dong Zhuo met the Young Emperor at Beimang and brought him back.

items.note: 甘肃文县与四川青川、平武之间的山岭，阴平道越此南下。

e.note: The ridge between Wen County in Gansu and Qingchuan and Pingwu in Sichuan; the Yinping Road crossed it going south.

items.note: 汉人称「幕」「大幕」，卫青、霍去病「绝幕」北击匈奴即穿越此漠。以「瀚海」专指戈壁是明代以后的事。

e.note: The Han called it the mu or the Great Mu; when Wei Qing and Huo Qubing 'crossed the mu' to strike north at the Xiongnu, this was the desert they crossed. 'Hanhai' became the standard name for the Gobi only from the Ming.

items.note: 沿斜水、褒水河谷开凿的栈道，长四百七十里，为关中通汉中的主道。诸葛亮 228 年扬言由此北出，234 年实由此出屯五丈原。

e.note: A plank road built along the valleys of the Ye and Bao rivers, 470 li long, the main route from Guanzhong to Hanzhong. In 228 Zhuge Liang announced that he would come north this way, and in 234 he actually did, camping at the Wuzhang Plains.

items.note: 长安正南出子午谷，经秦岭达汉中东部，路最近而最险。228 年魏延请率精兵五千由此奇袭长安，诸葛亮以为悬危未许；230 年曹真亦由此伐蜀，遇雨而还。

e.mod: south of Xi'an – east of Hanzhong, Shaanxi
e.note: It left Chang'an due south through the Ziwu Valley and crossed the Qinling to eastern Hanzhong: the shortest route and the most dangerous. In 228 Wei Yan asked to lead 5,000 picked troops this way to surprise Chang'an, but Zhuge Liang judged it too risky and refused; in 230 Cao Zhen also attacked Shu this way and turned back in the rain.

items.mod: 陕西宝鸡—凤县—略阳—勉县
items.note: 又称故道。出散关沿故道水南下，绕经武都东境至汉中，路远而平。215 年曹操征张鲁、228 年冬诸葛亮围陈仓皆经此道。

e.mod: Baoji – Feng County – Lüeyang – Mian County, Shaanxi
e.note: Also called the Gudao Road. It went out through San Pass and south along the Gudao River, curving through eastern Wudu to Hanzhong: long but level. Cao Cao's campaign against Zhang Lu in 215 and Zhuge Liang's siege of Chencang in winter 228 both went this way.

items.mod: 陕西勉县—甘肃礼县—天水
items.note: 自汉中西出，沿西汉水河谷北上至祁山，再出天水。道路较平缓、便于运粮，又可联络陇右羌氐，诸葛亮第一、四次北伐皆取此道。

e.mod: Mian County, Shaanxi – Li County – Tianshui, Gansu
e.note: It went west from Hanzhong and north up the Xihan River valley to Mount Qi, then out to Tianshui. The road was fairly gentle and easy for moving grain, and it allowed the army to link up with the Qiang and Di of Longyou; Zhuge Liang took it on his first and fourth northern campaigns.

items.mod: 陕西勉县—四川广元—剑阁—成都
items.note: 汉中经剑阁通成都的主道，相传秦惠王以石牛诈称能便金而开。263 年钟会大军沿此南下，受阻于剑阁。

e.mod: Mian County, Shaanxi – Guangyuan – Jiange – Chengdu, Sichuan
e.note: The main route from Hanzhong through Jiange to Chengdu; legend says it was opened when King Hui of Qin tricked Shu with stone oxen that supposedly dropped gold. In 263 Zhong Hui's army marched south along it and was stopped at Jiange.

items.note: 汉中越米仓山南下巴中的道路。215 年张鲁由此奔巴中，张郃随后南下宕渠，被张飞击退。

e.note: The route from Hanzhong over the Micang Mountains south to Bazhong. In 215 Zhang Lu fled this way to Bazhong; Zhang He later pushed south to Dangqu and was beaten back by Zhang Fei.

items.note: 207 年夏雨水泛滥、滨海道路不通，曹操用田畴之计出卢龙塞，循断绝二百年的古道，“堑山堙谷五百余里”，经白檀、平冈直趋柳城，乌桓猝不及防。

e.note: In summer 207 floods made the coast road impassable, so Cao Cao took Tian Chou's advice, went out through Lulong Fort and followed an old road disused for two hundred years, "cutting through mountains and filling valleys for more than 500 li", by way of Baitan and Pinggang straight to Liucheng, catching the Wuhuan off guard.

items.mod: 河南新安东（汉函谷关遗址）
items.note: 前114 年（元鼎三年），杨仆（后为楼船将军）耻为关外民，请以家财东移关城，武帝遂徙关于新安，去故关三百里，为洛阳西面门户；故关在今灵宝，改置弘农县（见灵宝的函谷关）。

e.mod: east of Xin'an, Henan (Han Hangu Pass site)
e.note: In 114 BC Yang Pu (later General of the Towered Ships), ashamed that his home lay outside the pass, asked to have it moved east at his own expense, and Emperor Wu moved it to Xin'an, three hundred li east of the old one; it became the western gateway to Luoyang. The old pass, at today's Lingbao, became the county of Hongnong (see the Hangu Pass at Lingbao).

items.note: 关中东南门户，通南阳、荆襄。

e.note: The southeastern gateway of Guanzhong, leading to Nanyang and Jing–Xiang.

items.note: 陈仓道（故道）北口。215 年曹操由此征张鲁，228 年冬诸葛亮由此出围陈仓。

e.note: Northern entrance of the Chencang Road (Gudao Road). Cao Cao went this way against Zhang Lu in 215, and Zhuge Liang came out this way to besiege Chencang in winter 228.

items.note: 陇山东麓关口，关中通陇右的要道。

e.note: The pass at the eastern foot of the Long Mountains, on the main road from Guanzhong to Longyou.

items.note: 关中通往安定、北地的门户。

e.note: The gateway from Guanzhong to Anding and Beidi.

items.mod: 陕西勉县西（汉代阳平关）
items.note: 汉中西面门户，又称阳安关。215 年曹操于此破张卫，217—219 年刘备与夏侯渊相持于此，263 年钟会遣胡烈攻破此关。

e.mod: west of Mian County, Shaanxi (the Han-era Yangping Pass)
e.note: The western gateway of Hanzhong, also called Yang'an Pass. Cao Cao broke Zhang Wei here in 215, Liu Bei faced Xiahou Yuan here from 217 to 219, and in 263 Zhong Hui sent Hu Lie to take the pass.

items.mod: 四川青川东北（地望有争议）
items.note: 益州北面要隘，刘璋使杨怀、高沛守之；212 年刘备斩二将夺关南下。

e.note: The key pass on the northern edge of Yi Province, held for Liu Zhang by Yang Huai and Gao Pei; in 212 Liu Bei beheaded the two commanders, took the pass and marched south.

items.note: 西汉水北岸孤峰，扼陇右通汉中的要道。诸葛亮第一、四次北伐皆出祁山，演义附会为“六出祁山”。

e.mod: east of Li County, Gansu (Qishan Fort)
e.note: A lone peak on the north bank of the Xihan River, guarding the main route from Longyou to Hanzhong. Zhuge Liang came out by Mount Qi on his first and fourth northern campaigns; the Romance stretches this into "six sorties from Mount Qi".

items.note: 即成皋关，洛阳东面门户，其西旋门关为汉末洛阳八关之一。演义“三英战吕布”安排在此，正史中讨董联军并未在此与吕布交战。

e.note: That is, Chenggao Pass, the eastern gateway of Luoyang; Xuanmen Pass to its west was one of the Eight Passes of Luoyang in the late Han. The Romance sets "the three heroes fight Lü Bu" here, but in the histories the coalition against Dong Zhuo never fought Lü Bu here.

items.note: 洛阳南面门户，汉末八关之一。

e.note: The southern gateway of Luoyang, one of the Eight Passes of Luoyang in the late Han.

items.note: 洛阳东南经嵩山通颍川的要道，汉末八关之一。

e.mod: southeast of Yanshi District, Luoyang, Henan
e.note: The route southeast from Luoyang past Mount Songgao to Yingchuan, one of the Eight Passes of Luoyang in the late Han.

items.note: 洛阳北面黄河渡口，含小平津，汉末八关之一。189 年张让等劫少帝出逃至此，投河自尽。

e.mod: northeast of Mengjin District, Luoyang, Henan
e.note: The Yellow River crossing north of Luoyang, including Xiaoping Ford, one of the Eight Passes of Luoyang in the late Han. In 189 Zhang Rang and the other eunuchs abducted the Young Emperor and fled here, then drowned themselves in the river.

items.note: 太行山陉道西口，上党东面门户。206 年高幹据此拒曹。

e.note: The western end of a defile through the Taihang Mountains and the eastern gateway of Shangdang. In 206 Gao Gan held it against Cao Cao.

items.mod: 河北石家庄鹿泉区西（土门关）
items.note: 太行八陉之一，河北通并州的要道。

e.mod: west of Luquan District, Shijiazhuang, Hebei (Tumen Pass)
e.note: One of the Eight Defiles of the Taihang, the main route from Hebei to Bing Province.

items.mod: 山西代县西北（雁门关一带）
items.note: 并州北门，又称西陉。

e.mod: northwest of Dai County, Shanxi (Yanmen Pass area)
e.note: The northern gate of Bing Province, also called the Western Defile.

items.note: 燕山西段要隘。

e.note: A key pass in the western Yan Mountains.

items.mod: 河北迁西北（喜峰口一带）
items.note: 燕山东段关隘，经此可出塞直趋柳城。207 年曹操用田畴之计由此奇袭乌桓。

e.note: A pass in the eastern Yan Mountains, from which one could go beyond the frontier straight to Liucheng. In 207 Cao Cao followed Tian Chou's plan and made his surprise attack on the Wuhuan this way.

items.mod: 甘肃敦煌西北（小方盘城）
items.note: 汉代通西域北道的关口，与阳关合称两关。设关年代与关址都有争议：一说前111 年前后筑塞至酒泉时初置，在敦煌以东——前103 年李广利首伐大宛不利，武帝「使使遮玉门」，军有敢入者斩，李广利只得留在敦煌，可见关仍在敦煌以东，此后才西移；一说自始即在敦煌西北。点位取小方盘城（玉门都尉治所）。

e.note: The Han pass on the Northern Route of the Western Regions. Together with the Yang Pass it made up the 'two passes'. Both its date and its site are disputed. On one view it was first set up around 111 BC, when the frontier was extended to Jiuquan, and lay east of Dunhuang: when Li Guangli's first campaign against Dayuan failed in 103 BC, Emperor Wu 'sent envoys to block the Yumen Pass' with orders to behead any soldier who dared to enter, and Li Guangli had to stay at Dunhuang, so the pass was still east of it; only later was it moved west. On another view it stood north-west of Dunhuang from the start. The map marker is placed at the Xiaofangpan fort, seat of the Chief Commandant of Yumen.

items.note: 汉代通西域南道的关口。与玉门关同为敦煌郡西境的两关，即「列四郡，据两关」；设置年代与玉门关一样有争议。

e.note: The Han pass on the Southern Route of the Western Regions. With the Yumen Pass it formed the 'two passes' on the western edge of Dunhuang Commandery — in the Hanshu's words, Han 'set up four commanderies and held the two passes'; like the Yumen Pass, its founding date is disputed.

items.note: 长江出三峡后的门户，荆门山在南岸、虎牙山在北岸。吴于此横江设铁锁，280 年被王濬烧断。

e.note: The gateway of the Yangtze as it leaves the Three Gorges, with Mount Jingmen on the south bank and Mount Huya on the north. Wu stretched iron chains across the river here, which Wang Jun burned through in 280.

items.note: 前119 年霍去病破左贤王，于此「封」（筑坛祭天）。一般认为即今蒙古国肯特山，也有在今内蒙古境内诸说。

e.note: Where Huo Qubing performed the feng sacrifice to Heaven in 119 BC after crushing the Wise King of the Left. Usually identified with the Khentii Mountains in Mongolia, though some place it in today's Inner Mongolia.

items.mod: 地望不详，在狼居胥山附近
items.note: 霍去病封狼居胥后「禅于姑衍」（除地祭地）。今地不详，一般认为在狼居胥山附近，图上为示意。

e.note: After the sacrifice on Mount Langjuxu, Huo Qubing performed the shan sacrifice to Earth on Mount Guyan. Its modern location is unknown; it is generally placed near Mount Langjuxu, and the map shows it only schematically.

items.note: 汉代的燕然山。89 年窦宪大破北单于后登此山，令班固作铭、刻石记功；2017 年中蒙联合考察队在蒙古国中戈壁省德勒格尔杭爱的山崖上辨认出《封燕然山铭》摩崖，燕然山的位置由此确定。

e.note: The Han dynasty's Mount Yanran. Dou Xian climbed it in 89 after crushing the northern chanyu and had Ban Gu's inscription carved here; in 2017 a joint Chinese–Mongolian survey identified the cliff inscription at Delgerkhangai in Dundgovi Province, Mongolia, fixing where Mount Yanran was.

items.note: 河西走廊中段，山丹、永昌之间。前121 年春霍去病过焉支山千余里。匈奴失此山，歌曰「失我焉支山，使我妇女无颜色」。

e.note: In the middle of the Hexi Corridor, between Shandan and Yongchang. In the spring of 121 BC Huo Qubing pressed more than a thousand li past it. Losing it, the Xiongnu sang, 'We have lost our Mount Yanzhi, and our women have lost their colour.'

items.note: 霍去病封狼居胥、禅姑衍之后「登临翰海」而还。翰海所指说法不一：一说即贝加尔湖，一说呼伦湖，一说杭爱山，也有人认为泛指漠北的大湖；图上取贝加尔湖说。后世「饮马瀚海」即用此典；以「瀚海」专指戈壁沙漠是明代以后的用法。

e.note: After the sacrifices on Mount Langjuxu and Mount Guyan, Huo Qubing 'climbed to look out over the Hanhai' and turned back. What the Hanhai was is disputed: Lake Baikal, Lake Hulun and the Khangai Mountains have all been proposed, and some take it as any great lake beyond the Gobi; the map follows the Lake Baikal view. Later writers' 'watering horses at the Hanhai' alludes to this; using 'Hanhai' as the standard name for the Gobi dates only from the Ming.

items.note: 秦都。始皇徙天下豪富十二万户于咸阳，渭南营阿房宫；前206 年为项羽所焚。

e.note: The Qin capital. The First Emperor moved 120,000 wealthy households here and began the Epang Palace south of the Wei; Xiang Yu burned it in 206 BC.

items.note: 陈胜张楚之都。

e.note: Capital of Chen Sheng's Zhang Chu.

items.note: 前208 年楚怀王徙都于此；前206 年为西楚霸王项羽之都。

e.note: King Huai of Chu moved his court here in 208 BC; from 206 BC it was the capital of Xiang Yu, Hegemon-King of Western Chu.

items.note: 汉王刘邦初都。

e.note: First capital of Liu Bang as king of Han.

items.note: 秦献公旧都。汉王还定三秦后都此，前200 年长乐宫成，徙都长安。

e.note: The old capital of Duke Xian of Qin. The king of Han made it his capital after retaking the Three Qins, moving to Chang'an when the Changle Palace was finished in 200 BC.

items.mod: 陕西西安西北（汉长安城）
items.note: 西汉都城。萧何营未央宫，惠帝筑城，城周六十余里；武帝起建章宫、凿昆明池。

e.mod: northwest of Xi'an, Shaanxi (Han Chang'an city)
e.note: The Western Han capital. Xiao He built the Weiyang Palace and Emperor Hui the walls, over sixty li round; Emperor Wu added the Jianzhang Palace and dug the Kunming Pool.

items.note: 王莽改长安为常安，为新都。

e.note: Wang Mang changed the first character of Chang'an's name (长 to 常; the sound is unchanged) and made it the Xin capital.

items.mod: 河南洛阳东（汉魏洛阳故城）
items.note: 25 年光武定都于此，是为东汉；城南北九里、东西六里，号「九六城」。

e.mod: east of Luoyang, Henan (Han–Wei city site)
e.note: Emperor Guangwu made it his capital in 25, founding the Eastern Han; the city, nine li north to south and six east to west, was nicknamed the 'nine-six city'.

items.note: 田齐故都，秦末诸田复国都此。

e.note: The old Tian Qi capital, where the Tian family re-established Qi at the end of Qin.

items.note: 赵歇所都；项羽改名襄国，封张耳为常山王都此。

e.note: Zhao Xie's capital; Xiang Yu renamed it Xiangguo and gave it to Zhang Er as king of Changshan.

items.note: 燕国故都。

e.note: The old Yan capital.

items.note: 秦南海郡治，赵佗南越国都。1983 年发现南越王墓（文帝赵眜）。

e.note: Seat of Qin's Nanhai Commandery and capital of Zhao Tuo's Nanyue; the tomb of Zhao Mo, Emperor Wen of Nanyue, was found in 1983.

items.note: 闽越王无诸都城。

e.note: Capital of Wuzhu, king of Minyue.

items.note: 东海王摇都城，俗称东瓯。

e.note: Capital of Yao, king of Donghai, commonly called Dong'ou.

items.note: 卫氏朝鲜都城；汉置乐浪郡朝鲜县。

e.old: The chanyu's court (south of the Gobi)
e.note: The chanyu's court, which moved with the water and pasture and had no fixed walls. Describing the lands of the kings under Modu, the Shiji says the kings and generals of the left lived in the east and those of the right in the west, 'and the chanyu's court faced Dai and Yunzhong': south of the Gobi, due north of Dai and Yunzhong commanderies. The sources give no exact site, so the point is only a sketch. After Zhao Xin went over to the Xiongnu in 123 BC, he advised the chanyu to move 'further north across the Gobi to lure the Han troops on and wear them out', and from then on the court lay north of the desert; after the battle beyond the Gobi in 119 BC 'there was no royal court south of the Gobi'.

items.note: 匈奴一年三会：正月诸长小会于单于庭；五月大会茏城，祭祖先、天地、鬼神；秋天马肥时大会蹛林，清点人口牲畜。前129 年卫青率万骑出上谷，直捣茏城，斩首虏七百，是汉主动出击匈奴的第一次胜利。《史记》作「茏城」，《汉书》作「龙城」；有学者认为卫青所到的茏城在漠南，与漠北的龙城不是一地，漠北远在当时汉军的作战范围之外。前123 年单于庭北迁以后，大会之所也随之移到漠北（见单于庭）。点位只按卫青出上谷的方向示意，今地无考。

e.mod: western Xilingol, Inner Mongolia (south of the Gobi; approx.)
e.note: The Xiongnu held three assemblies a year: the chiefs held a lesser assembly at the chanyu's court in the first month; in the fifth they held the great assembly at Longcheng and sacrificed to their ancestors, Heaven and Earth, and the spirits; and in autumn, when the horses were fat, they assembled at Dailin to count their people and herds. In 129 BC Wei Qing rode out from Shanggu with ten thousand horsemen, struck at Longcheng and took seven hundred heads and prisoners, Han's first victory on the offensive against the Xiongnu. The Shiji and the Hanshu write the name with different characters, and some scholars hold that the Longcheng Wei Qing reached lay south of the Gobi and was not the Longcheng north of it, which was far beyond the reach of Han armies at the time. After the chanyu's court moved north in 123 BC, the great assembly moved north of the Gobi with it (see the chanyu's court). The point only follows Wei Qing's line of march from Shanggu; the modern site is unknown.

items.mod: 蒙古国后杭爱省鄂尔浑河中游（大致）
items.note: 前123 年赵信劝单于「益北绝幕」以后的单于庭，在大漠以北。前119 年卫青出定襄绝幕，与单于会战，追至窴颜山赵信城；此后「幕南无王庭」。前105 年儿单于立，「单于益西北」。王庭随水草迁徙，正月诸长小会于此，五月大会龙城。考古上，后杭爱省鄂尔浑河与塔米尔河交汇一带有两处候选：2014—2018 年中蒙联合发掘的和日门塔拉「三连城」，内城不见居住痕迹，发掘者认为可能是史籍所记祭祀、会盟的龙城；2020 年蒙古学者在交汇处以北约 27 公里的城址出土「天子单于」瓦当，认为即龙城。也有学者认为后者是单于庭、三连城才是龙城。48 年匈奴分裂后为北单于庭；89 年窦宪破北单于于稽落山，91 年耿夔出居延塞，围北单于于金微山，北单于逃走，不知所在，王庭从此不在漠北。点位取鄂尔浑河中游，只是大致。

e.note: The chanyu's court after 123 BC, when Zhao Xin advised the chanyu to move 'further north across the Gobi'. In 119 BC Wei Qing crossed the Gobi from Dingxiang, fought the chanyu and pursued him as far as Zhao Xin's fort at Mount Tianyan; after that 'there was no royal court south of the Gobi'. After the boy chanyu came to the throne in 105 BC, 'the chanyu moved further north-west'. The court moved with the water and pasture; the chiefs held a lesser assembly here in the first month, and the great assembly met at Longcheng in the fifth. Archaeology offers two candidates where the Orkhon and Tamir rivers meet in Arkhangai: the 'triple town' of Khermen Tal, excavated by a joint Chinese–Mongolian team in 2014–2018, whose inner enclosure shows no sign of habitation and which its excavators think may be the Longcheng of the sources, the place of sacrifices and assemblies; and a walled site about 27 km north of the confluence, where Mongolian archaeologists found eaves tiles reading 'Son of Heaven, the chanyu' in 2020 and which they take to be Longcheng. Some scholars hold instead that the latter was the chanyu's court and the triple town Longcheng. After the Xiongnu split in AD 48 it was the court of the northern chanyu; in 89 Dou Xian defeated the northern chanyu at Mount Jiluo, and in 91 Geng Kui marched out of the Juyan frontier and surrounded him in the Jinwei Mountains, from where he fled and was lost track of. After that there was no royal court north of the Gobi. The point on the middle Orkhon is only approximate.

items.note: 前51 年呼韩邪单于入朝甘泉宫，称臣于汉；归国时「自请愿留居光禄塞下，有急保汉受降城」。汉遣董忠、韩昌率骑一万六千送单于出朔方鸡鹿塞，留下护卫，前后转运边谷三万四千斛供其食用。光禄城是前102 年徐自为所筑五原塞外列城之一，《汉书·地理志》说由稒阳「北出石门障得光禄城」。这时漠北的单于庭为郅支单于所据，郅支后来西迁坚昆、康居；呼韩邪部众日渐恢复，「塞下禽兽尽」，大臣多劝北归，约前43 年回到单于庭。点位只按光禄塞示意。

e.note: In 51 BC the chanyu Huhanye came to court at the Ganquan Palace and acknowledged himself a subject of Han; on leaving he 'asked to stay by the Guanglu frontier and, in an emergency, to take refuge in the Han fort of Shouxiang'. Han sent Dong Zhong and Han Chang with sixteen thousand horsemen to escort him out through the Jilu frontier post in Shuofang and stay on to guard him, and supplied him with 34,000 hu of grain from the frontier commanderies in all. Guanglu was one of the line of forts that Xu Ziwei built beyond the Wuyuan frontier in 102 BC; the treatise on geography in the Hanshu, under Guyang County, reaches it by going 'north out through the Shimen barrier'. Meanwhile the court north of the Gobi was held by the chanyu Zhizhi, who later moved west to the Jiankun and the Kangju. As Huhanye's people recovered and 'the game along the frontier was hunted out', his ministers urged him to go back north, and around 43 BC he returned to the chanyu's court. The marker is placed at the Guanglu frontier and is only approximate.

items.note: 48 年匈奴南边八部共立日逐王比为呼韩邪单于，附汉。50 年汉遣中郎将段郴、副校尉王郁「立其庭，去五原西部塞八十里」；同年冬，南单于与北单于交战不利，诏令徙居西河郡美稷县，段郴、王郁留驻西河护卫（此后设使匈奴中郎将监护），南单于庭从此设在塞内，诸部分屯北边诸郡。此后南单于庭长期设在美稷；188 年羌渠单于被杀，其子於夫罗为国人所拒、不得归国，后留居河东平阳。美稷故城一说即准格尔旗纳林古城。

e.note: In AD 48 the eight southern Xiongnu tribes together made Bi, the Rizhu king, chanyu under the title Huhanye, and he submitted to Han. In 50 Han sent the General of the Household Duan Chen and the Deputy Colonel Wang Yu to 'set up his court eighty li from the western frontier of Wuyuan'; that winter, after the southern chanyu had fared badly against the northern chanyu, he was ordered to move to Meiji County in Xihe Commandery, and Duan Chen and Wang Yu stayed in Xihe to guard him (a General of the Household Emissary to the Xiongnu was later appointed to supervise him). From then on the southern chanyu's court lay inside the frontier, and his tribes were stationed across the northern commanderies. The court remained at Meiji for a long time; in 188 the chanyu Qiangqu was killed and his son Yufuluo was rejected by his own people, and, unable to return, he eventually settled at Pingyang in Hedong. The old town of Meiji is sometimes identified with the walled site of Nalin in Jungar Banner.

In summer he and Gongsun Ao set out from Beidi by separate roads; Gongsun Ao lost his way, and Huo Qubing went on alone past Juyan and through the Lesser Yuezhi lands to the Qilian Mountains, taking more than 30,000. In autumn the Hunye king killed the Xiutu king and surrendered, and Hexi passed to Han.
e.cmd: Huo Qubing vs. the Hunye and Xiutu kings

items.note: 卫青出定襄千余里，遇单于陈兵以待，以武刚车环为营，纵五千骑往击；日暮大风扬沙，汉益纵左右翼绕单于，单于与壮骑数百溃围西北遁，汉军追至窴颜山赵信城。霍去病出代二千余里，破左贤王，斩首虏七万余，封狼居胥山，禅于姑衍，登临翰海。李广失道后期，自刭。「是后匈奴远遁，而幕南无王庭。」此役之后二人不复出塞：卫青前后七出击匈奴，斩捕首虏五万余级；霍去病六出，其四出以将军，斩捕首虏十一万余级（《史记》）。
items.cmd: 卫青、霍去病 vs 伊稚斜单于、左贤王

e.note: More than a thousand li out of Dingxiang Wei Qing found the chanyu drawn up waiting; he circled his armoured wagons into a laager and loosed five thousand horse at him. At dusk a gale threw up the sand, Han sent its wings round the chanyu, and he broke out to the north-west with a few hundred picked riders; the Han army pursued him to Zhao Xin's fort at Mount Tianyan. Huo Qubing marched more than two thousand li from Dai, crushed the Wise King of the Left, took over 70,000 heads and prisoners, sacrificed to Heaven on Mount Langjuxu and to Earth on Mount Guyan and climbed to look out over the Hanhai. Li Guang lost his way, arrived too late and cut his own throat. 'After this the Xiongnu fled far away, and there was no royal court south of the desert.' Neither man took the field again: in all Wei Qing campaigned against the Xiongnu seven times, taking more than 50,000 heads and prisoners, and Huo Qubing six times, four of them as a general, taking more than 110,000 (Shiji).
e.cmd: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing vs. the chanyu Yizhixie and the Wise King of the Left

items.note: 楼船将军杨仆纵火烧城，伏波将军路博德招降，南越亡。
items.cmd: 路博德、杨仆 vs 吕嘉

e.note: Yang Pu, General of the Towered Ships, set the city on fire while Lu Bode, General Who Calms the Waves, took the surrender; Nanyue fell.
e.cmd: Lu Bode and Yang Pu vs. Lü Jia

items.note: 汉军水陆围城数月，朝鲜大臣杀右渠王来降。
items.cmd: 杨仆、荀彘 vs 右渠

e.note: Han forces besieged the city by land and sea for months until Joseon ministers killed King Ugeo and surrendered.
e.cmd: Yang Pu and Xun Zhi vs. Ugeo

items.note: 赵破奴以轻骑七百虏楼兰王，遂破车师。
items.sides: 汉 胜 楼兰·车师
items.cmd: 赵破奴、王恢

e.note: Zhao Ponu captured the king of Loulan with seven hundred light horsemen and went on to break Jushi.
e.cmd: Zhao Ponu and Wang Hui

items.note: 李广利围贵山城，断其水源，大宛贵人杀王出降，献汗血马。
items.cmd: 李广利 vs 毋寡

e.note: Li Guangli besieged Guishan and cut off its water until the nobles killed their king, surrendered and handed over the blood-sweating horses.
e.cmd: Li Guangli vs. Wugua

items.mod: 蒙古国南部（地望有争议）
items.note: 李陵以步卒五千深入，遇单于三万骑，转战八日，矢尽而降。
items.cmd: 且鞮侯单于 vs 李陵

e.note: Li Ling marched deep with five thousand foot and met the chanyu's 30,000 horsemen; after eight days of fighting his arrows ran out and he surrendered.
e.cmd: The chanyu Qiedihou vs. Li Ling

items.note: 李广利闻家族因巫蛊被收，冒进至郅居水，还至燕然山，军溃降匈奴。
items.cmd: 狐鹿姑单于 vs 李广利

e.note: Hearing his family had been arrested in the witchcraft affair, Li Guangli pushed recklessly on to the Zhiju River; on the way back, at Mount Yanran, his army broke and he surrendered to the Xiongnu.
e.cmd: The chanyu Hulugu vs. Li Guangli

items.mod: 哈萨克斯坦塔拉兹一带
items.note: 汉与西域诸国兵四万余攻破郅支城，斩单于。
items.cmd: 陈汤、甘延寿 vs 郅支单于

e.note: More than 40,000 Han and Western Regions troops stormed Zhizhi's fortress and beheaded the chanyu.
e.cmd: Chen Tang and Gan Yanshou vs. the chanyu Zhizhi

items.note: 刘秀以三千敢死士冲新军中坚，斩王寻，会大风雨，新军四十万溃散。
items.cmd: 刘秀 vs 王寻、王邑

e.note: Liu Xiu charged the Xin centre with three thousand men sworn to die and killed Wang Xun; in a great storm the 400,000-strong Xin army scattered.
e.cmd: Liu Xiu vs. Wang Xun and Wang Yi

items.note: 冯异令士卒以朱涂眉，混入赤眉阵中，大破之，降者八万。
items.cmd: 冯异 vs 樊崇

e.note: Feng Yi had his men paint their eyebrows red and mingle with the enemy, routing the Red Eyebrows; 80,000 surrendered.
e.cmd: Feng Yi vs. Fan Chong

items.note: 耿弇连拔祝阿、西安、临淄，大破张步，平齐地十二郡。
items.cmd: 耿弇 vs 张步

e.note: Geng Yan took Zhu'a, Xi'an (in Qi) and Linzi one after another, routed Zhang Bu and won the twelve commanderies of Qi.
e.cmd: Geng Yan vs. Zhang Bu

items.note: 来歙间道袭取略阳，隗嚣倾兵围攻数月不下，光武亲征。
items.cmd: 来歙 vs 隗嚣

e.note: Lai Xi seized Lüeyang by a hidden path; Wei Xiao besieged it with his whole army for months in vain, and the emperor came in person.
e.cmd: Lai Xi vs. Wei Xiao

items.note: 岑彭乘东风以楼船冲断浮桥，焚荆门、虎牙之栅，溯江入蜀。
items.cmd: 岑彭 vs 任满、田戎

e.cmd: Cen Peng vs. Ren Man and Tian Rong

items.note: 吴汉进逼成都，公孙述出战中创，夜死，成家亡。
items.cmd: 吴汉 vs 公孙述

e.note: Wu Han closed in on Chengdu; Gongsun Shu was wounded in a sortie and died that night, ending Chengjia.
e.cmd: Wu Han vs. Gongsun Shu

items.note: 马援缘海而进，随山刊道千余里，破征侧于浪泊，次年斩之。
items.cmd: 马援 vs 征侧、征贰

e.note: Ma Yuan advanced along the coast, cutting a road through the hills for over a thousand li, beat Trưng Trắc at Langbo and beheaded her the next year.
e.cmd: Ma Yuan vs. Trưng Trắc and Trưng Nhị

items.note: 窦固出酒泉，破呼衍王于天山，追至蒲类海，取伊吾卢地。
items.cmd: 窦固、耿忠 vs 呼衍王

e.note: Dou Gu marched from Jiuquan, beat the Huyan king in the Tianshan, pursued him to Lake Pulei and took the Yiwulu lands.
e.cmd: Dou Gu and Geng Zhong vs. the Huyan king

items.note: 窦固、耿秉、刘张出敦煌昆仑塞，破北匈奴于蒲类海上，遂入车师；耿秉先击车师后王，后王安得出门迎降，前王亦降。于是复置西域都护、戊己校尉。
items.cmd: 窦固、耿秉、刘张 vs 北匈奴

e.note: Dou Gu, Geng Bing and Liu Zhang set out from the Kunlun frontier post of Dunhuang, beat the Northern Xiongnu on the shore of Lake Pulei and entered Jushi; Geng Bing struck first at the Rear King, An'de, who came out of his gate to surrender, and the Front King submitted too. The Protector-General and the Wu-Ji colonels were then restored.
e.cmd: Dou Gu, Geng Bing and Liu Zhang vs. the Northern Xiongnu

items.note: 北匈奴与车师围戊己校尉耿恭于车师后部疏勒城，拜井得泉，坚守经年，生还者十三人。
items.cmd: 耿恭

e.note: The Northern Xiongnu and Jushi besieged the Wu-Ji colonel Geng Gong at the fort of Shule in the Rear Kingdom of Jushi; he found water by bowing to the well and held out for a year, only thirteen men surviving.
e.cmd: Geng Gong

items.note: 建初元年正月，酒泉太守段彭等发张掖、酒泉、敦煌三郡及鄯善兵七千余人，会柳中击车师，攻交河城，斩首三千八百级，北匈奴惊走，车师复降。己校尉关宠已没；范羌分兵二千越天山迎耿恭。章帝随即罢都护与戊己校尉。
items.cmd: 段彭、王蒙、皇甫援 vs 车师

e.note: In the 1st month of Jianchu 1 Duan Peng, Administrator of Jiuquan, and others gathered over 7,000 men from Zhangye, Jiuquan, Dunhuang and Shanshan at Liuzhong, attacked Jushi and stormed Jiaohe, taking 3,800 heads; the Northern Xiongnu fled and Jushi submitted again. The Ji colonel Guan Chong was already dead; Fan Qiang took 2,000 men over the Tianshan to bring out Geng Gong. Emperor Zhang then abolished the Protector-General and the Wu-Ji colonels.
e.cmd: Duan Peng, Wang Meng and Huangfu Yuan vs. Jushi

items.mod: 蒙古国南戈壁一带（地望有争议）

items.sides: 汉·南匈奴 胜 北匈奴
items.cmd: 窦宪、耿秉 vs 北单于

e.sides: Han and the Southern Xiongnu defeated the Northern Xiongnu
e.cmd: Dou Xian and Geng Bing vs. the northern chanyu

items.note: 汉军出居延塞五千余里，围北单于于金微山，北单于西走。
items.cmd: 耿夔、任尚 vs 北单于

e.note: The Han army marched over five thousand li from the Juyan frontier and surrounded the northern chanyu at the Jinwei Mountains; he fled west.
e.cmd: Geng Kui and Ren Shang vs. the northern chanyu

items.cmd: 班超 vs 焉耆王广
