e.cmd: Ban Chao vs. Guang, king of Karasahr

items.note: 先零羌大破汉军于平襄，死者八千余人，滇零自称天子于北地。
items.cmd: 滇零 vs 任尚

e.note: The Xianlian Qiang crushed the Han army at Pingxiang, killing over eight thousand, and Dianlian proclaimed himself Son of Heaven in Beidi.
e.cmd: Dianling vs. Ren Shang

items.note: 班勇发龟兹、姑墨、温宿兵万余人至车师前王庭，击走北匈奴伊蠡王，前部复通。
items.cmd: 班勇 vs 伊蠡王

e.note: Ban Yong raised over ten thousand troops from Kucha, Gumo and Wensu, marched to the court of the Front King of Jushi and drove off the Northern Xiongnu Yili king, reopening the Front Kingdom.
e.cmd: Ban Yong vs. the Yili king

items.note: 段颎分兵夹击，东羌一万九千级授首，东羌平。
items.cmd: 段颎 vs 东羌

e.note: Duan Jiong attacked from both sides, taking 19,000 heads; the Eastern Qiang were put down.
e.cmd: Duan Jiong vs. the Eastern Qiang

items.note: 汉三道出塞二千余里，为鲜卑所败，死者十七八。
items.cmd: 檀石槐 vs 夏育、田晏、臧旻

e.note: Three Han columns marched over two thousand li beyond the frontier and were routed by the Xianbei, seven or eight in ten killed.
e.cmd: Tanshihuai vs. Xia Yu, Tian Yan and Zang Min

items.note: 前213 年用李斯议焚《诗》《书》百家语；次年坑诸生四百六十余人于咸阳。

e.old: Burning of the books, burying of the scholars
e.note: In 213 BC, on Li Si's advice, the Odes, the Documents and the works of the hundred schools were burned; the next year more than 460 scholars were buried at Xianyang.

items.note: 始皇东巡崩于沙丘平台，赵高、李斯秘不发丧，矫诏赐死扶苏，立胡亥。

e.note: The First Emperor died on tour at Shaqiu; Zhao Gao and Li Si concealed his death, forged an order for Fusu to kill himself and enthroned Huhai.

items.note: 陈胜、吴广遇雨失期，「王侯将相宁有种乎」，斩尉起事，为秦末首义。

e.note: Late because of the rain, Chen Sheng and Wu Guang killed their officers ('are kings, lords, generals and ministers born to it?') — the first rising against Qin.

items.note: 刘邦入咸阳后还军霸上，与关中父老约法三章：杀人者死，伤人及盗抵罪，余悉除去秦法。

e.note: Back at Bashang after entering Xianyang, Liu Bang agreed three articles with the elders of Guanzhong — death for murder, punishment for injury and theft — abolishing the rest of Qin law.

items.note: 项羽设宴鸿门，范增使项庄舞剑欲杀刘邦，项伯翼蔽，樊哙闯帐，刘邦脱身。

e.note: At Xiang Yu's banquet at Hongmen, Fan Zeng had Xiang Zhuang perform a sword dance to kill Liu Bang; Xiang Bo shielded him, Fan Kuai burst in and Liu Bang got away.

items.note: 项羽屠咸阳，杀子婴，烧秦宫室，火三月不灭。

e.note: Xiang Yu sacked Xianyang, killed Ziying and burned the Qin palaces; the fire was not put out for three months.

items.note: 项羽至乌江，「天之亡我，我何渡为」，自刎而死。

e.note: Reaching Wujiang, Xiang Yu said 'Heaven is destroying me — why should I cross?' and cut his own throat.

items.note: 吕后与萧何诱韩信入长乐宫钟室斩之，夷三族。

e.note: Empress Lü and Xiao He lured Han Xin into the bell room of the Changle Palace and executed him with three branches of his family.

items.note: 汉伏兵三十万于马邑欲诱击单于，事泄未果，和亲遂绝。

e.note: Han hid 300,000 men at Mayi to ambush the chanyu, but the plan leaked; the peace by marriage ended.

items.note: 主父偃献策：许诸侯王推私恩分封子弟为侯，王国由是自析。

e.note: On Zhufu Yan's proposal kings were allowed to grant parts of their lands to younger sons as marquisates, so the kingdoms divided themselves.

items.note: 张骞去十三年，百余人仅二人得还，备言西域诸国之地形物产，史称「凿空」。

e.note: Zhang Qian came back after thirteen years, only two of more than a hundred men surviving, with full reports on the terrain and products of the states of the Western Regions — the 'opening of the void'.

items.note: 桑弘羊等主持盐铁官营、均输平准、算缗告缗，以济边用。

e.note: Sang Hongyang and others set up state monopolies of salt and iron, equitable transport and price stabilisation, and taxes on merchants to pay for the frontier wars.

items.note: 江充诬太子刘据行巫蛊，太子发兵诛江充，兵败自杀，死者数万。

e.note: Jiang Chong accused Crown Prince Liu Ju of witchcraft; the prince raised troops and killed him but was defeated and killed himself, tens of thousands dying.

items.note: 武帝晚年下诏罢轮台屯田，「当今务在禁苛暴，止擅赋，力本农」。

e.note: In his last years Emperor Wu issued an edict dropping the farming garrison at Luntai: 'our task now is to stop harshness, end arbitrary levies and devote ourselves to farming'.

items.note: 贤良文学与桑弘羊辩论盐铁官营存废，桓宽录为《盐铁论》。

e.note: Scholars debated with Sang Hongyang whether to keep the salt and iron monopolies; Huan Kuan recorded it as the Discourses on Salt and Iron.

items.note: 汉发十五万骑与乌孙夹击匈奴，常惠率乌孙兵获单于父行、嫂、居次。

e.note: Han sent 150,000 horsemen to attack the Xiongnu together with Wusun; Chang Hui and the Wusun captured the chanyu's uncles, sister-in-law and daughters.

items.note: 宣帝召诸儒于石渠阁讲论五经同异，亲称制临决。

e.note: Emperor Xuan gathered the scholars at the Shiqu Pavilion to debate differences among the Five Classics, deciding the questions himself.

items.note: 元帝以宫人王嫱嫁呼韩邪单于，号宁胡阏氏，汉匈和亲六十余年。

e.old: Wang Zhaojun goes beyond the frontier
e.note: Emperor Yuan gave the palace lady Wang Qiang to the chanyu Huhanye as a bride, titled Ninghu Yanzhi; Han and the Xiongnu stayed at peace for over sixty years.

items.note: 王田、私属，五均六筦，屡改币制，改官名地名，扰民尤甚。

e.note: Nationalised land, a ban on selling slaves, price controls and monopolies, repeated changes of coinage and of official and place names — all deeply disruptive.

items.note: 河决魏郡，东南流经清河以东数郡入海，王莽以元城祖坟无水患而不塞，泛滥近六十年。

e.note: The river broke its banks in Wei Commandery and flowed south-east through several commanderies east of Qinghe to the sea; Wang Mang left the breach open because his ancestral tombs at Yuancheng were safe, and the floods went on for nearly sixty years.

items.note: 刘秀即皇帝位于鄗南千秋亭，改元建武。

e.note: Liu Xiu took the throne at the Qianqiu Pavilion south of Hao, with the era name Jianwu.

items.note: 马援平交趾后立铜柱为汉之极界（传说）。

e.note: After pacifying Jiaozhi Ma Yuan is said to have set up bronze pillars at the limit of Han territory.

items.note: 倭奴国遣使奉贡，光武赐以印绶；1784 年志贺岛出土「汉委奴国王」金印。

e.old: The Wa state of Na sends tribute
e.note: The Wa state of Na sent envoys and Emperor Guangwu gave it a seal; the gold seal 'King of Na of Wa of Han' was found on Shikanoshima in 1784.

items.note: 明帝遣使求法，迦叶摩腾、竺法兰以白马驮经至洛阳，建白马寺。

e.note: Emperor Ming sent envoys to seek the Buddhist teaching; Kasyapa Matanga and Dharmaratna brought scriptures to Luoyang on a white horse, and the White Horse Temple was built.

items.note: 王景、王吴发卒数十万修汴渠、筑河堤千余里，黄河自此安流八百年。

e.old: Wang Jing tames the Yellow River
e.note: Wang Jing and Wang Wu led hundreds of thousands of workers to restore the Bian Canal and build over a thousand li of dykes; the river then flowed quietly for eight hundred years.

items.note: 班超遣甘英出使大秦，经安息至条支海滨，闻海广难渡而还。

e.old: Gan Ying's mission to Da Qin
e.note: Ban Chao sent Gan Ying towards Da Qin; he crossed Parthia to the shore of the sea of Tiaozhi but turned back, told it was too wide to cross.

items.note: 尚方令蔡伦用树皮、麻头、敝布、鱼网造纸，奏上，「天下咸称蔡侯纸」。

e.note: Cai Lun, director of the imperial workshops, made paper from bark, hemp waste, rags and fishing nets and presented it; 'everyone called it Marquis Cai's paper'.

items.note: 以班勇为西域长史，屯柳中，代行都护之职。

e.old: Chief Clerk of the Western Regions
e.note: Ban Yong was made Chief Clerk of the Western Regions, garrisoned at Liuzhong and acting in place of a Protector-General.

items.note: 太史令张衡作候风地动仪，138 年测得陇西地震。

e.note: Zhang Heng, the Grand Astrologer, built his seismoscope, which detected an earthquake in Longxi in 138.

items.note: 且冻、傅难羌反，寇三辅，烧园陵，杀长吏，历五年乃平。

e.note: The Qiedong and Funan Qiang rebelled, raiding the capital region, burning imperial tombs and killing officials; it took five years to suppress.

items.note: 宦官诬李膺等结党，禁锢终身；169 年再兴党狱，死者百余人。

e.note: The eunuchs accused Li Ying and others of forming factions and barred them from office for life; a second purge in 169 killed over a hundred.

items.note: 蔡邕等正定六经文字，刻石立于太学门外。

e.note: Cai Yong and others fixed the texts of the Six Classics, carved them in stone and set them up outside the Imperial Academy.

items.mod: 甘肃兰州以北黄河西岸一带（大致）
items.note: 单于怒浑邪王屡败，欲诛之；浑邪王与休屠王谋降汉，休屠王中悔，浑邪王杀之，并其众。霍去病渡河受降，浑邪王部众多欲遁去，霍去病驰入营中斩欲亡者八千人，降者四万余，号称十万，汉分处于五郡塞外为五属国。休屠王太子金日磾没入官养马，后为武帝顾命大臣。

e.mod: west bank of the Yellow River north of Lanzhou, Gansu (approx.)
e.note: The chanyu, furious at the Hunye king's repeated defeats, meant to have him killed; the Hunye king plotted with the Xiutu king to go over to Han, and when the Xiutu king had second thoughts he killed him and took his people. Huo Qubing crossed the Yellow River to receive the surrender; when many of the Hunye king's men tried to slip away, he rode into their camp and cut down eight thousand of them. More than 40,000 surrendered (it was given out as 100,000) and were settled beyond the frontier of five commanderies as five dependent states. The Xiutu king's heir, Jin Midi, was made a palace slave tending horses and later became one of the ministers Emperor Wu named on his deathbed.

items.note: 霍去病破左贤王，封狼居胥山，禅于姑衍，登临翰海。封是筑土为坛祭天，禅是除地祭地，本是天子告成功的大礼；霍去病以此宣示汉兵所至。「封狼居胥」从此成为武将功业的最高象征，辛弃疾「元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾」即用此典。

e.note: Having crushed the Wise King of the Left, Huo Qubing performed the feng sacrifice to Heaven on Mount Langjuxu and the shan sacrifice to Earth on Mount Guyan, then climbed to look out over the Hanhai. Feng meant raising an earth altar to Heaven and shan clearing the ground to sacrifice to Earth, rites by which a Son of Heaven announced his achievements; Huo Qubing used them to proclaim how far Han arms had reached. 'Sacrificing on Langjuxu' became the supreme emblem of a general's success, and Xin Qiji's line on the hasty Yuanjia expedition that dreamed of Langjuxu and ended in a panicked retreat draws on it.

items.note: 前100 年中郎将苏武持节出使匈奴，因副使张胜参与谋劫单于母阏氏事被扣。单于幽之大窖中，苏武啮雪与旃毛并咽之，数日不死；乃徙北海上无人处，使牧羝（公羊），曰「羝乳乃得归」。苏武杖汉节牧羊，卧起操持，节旄尽落。前81 年汉匈和亲，汉使以「天子射上林中得雁，足有系帛书」诘单于，苏武始得归，留匈奴凡十九年。

e.note: In 100 BC Su Wu, a General of the Household, went to the Xiongnu as envoy bearing the emperor's tally, and was detained when his deputy Zhang Sheng was implicated in a plot to kidnap the chanyu's mother. Shut in a cellar, Su Wu chewed snow and swallowed felt and survived for days; he was then sent to an empty land by the North Sea to herd rams and told he could go home when they gave milk. He herded them leaning on the Han tally, holding it waking and sleeping until all its tassels had fallen off. When Han and the Xiongnu made peace in 81 BC, a Han envoy confronted the chanyu with the tale that the emperor had shot a wild goose in the Shanglin park with a silk letter tied to its foot, and Su Wu was at last allowed home after nineteen years among the Xiongnu.

items.mod: 蒙古国中戈壁省德勒格尔杭爱
items.note: 窦宪大破北单于后登燕然山，去塞三千余里，令中护军班固作《封燕然山铭》，刻石勒功。摩崖于 1990 年代为当地人发现，2017 年中蒙联合考察队释读确认，「勒石燕然」从此有了确切的地点。

e.note: After crushing the northern chanyu, Dou Xian climbed Mount Yanran, more than three thousand li beyond the frontier, and had his army protector Ban Gu compose the Inscription for the Feng Sacrifice on Mount Yanran, which was carved into the rock. The cliff inscription was found by local people in the 1990s and identified by a joint Chinese–Mongolian survey in 2017, giving 'carving the rock at Yanran' a precise place on the map.

items.mod: 河南荥阳—开封一带鸿沟沿线
items.note: 楚汉相持数月，楚兵罢食绝，韩信又进击楚。项羽与汉约，「中分天下，割鸿沟以西者为汉，鸿沟而东者为楚」，归还太公、吕后，解而东归。汉王欲西归，张良、陈平以为「此天亡楚之时也」，劝其背约追击。

e.mod: along the Honggou between Xingyang and Kaifeng, Henan
e.note: After months of stalemate, with the Chu army exhausted, its food gone and Han Xin advancing on Chu, Xiang Yu agreed with Han to 'divide the realm in two, the land west of the Honggou to Han and the land east of it to Chu', handed back the king of Han's father and wife and marched away east. The king of Han meant to go back west, but Zhang Liang and Chen Ping told him that 'this is the moment Heaven has chosen to destroy Chu' and urged him to break the agreement and pursue.

items.note: 贝加尔湖以南的游牧部族，冒顿时服属匈奴，东汉时屡击北匈奴。

e.note: Nomads south of Lake Baikal, subject to the Xiongnu under Modu; under the Eastern Han they often attacked the Northern Xiongnu.

items.note: 叶尼塞河上游的部族（后之黠戛斯），郅支单于曾徙居其地。

e.note: A people of the upper Yenisei (later the Kyrgyz), among whom the chanyu Zhizhi once lived.

items.note: 阿尔泰山南麓的部族，前176 年服属匈奴。

e.note: A people of the southern Altai, subject to the Xiongnu from 176 BC.

items.note: 河套东北的部族，汉初并于匈奴，前127 年为卫青所逐。

e.note: A people north-east of the Ordos, absorbed by the Xiongnu in early Han and driven out by Wei Qing in 127 BC.

items.note: 河套的部族，号白羊王，前127 年为卫青所逐。

e.note: A people of the Ordos under the Baiyang king, driven out by Wei Qing in 127 BC.

items.note: 月氏西迁时留居南山的余部，与羌杂处，东汉时为湟中义从胡。

e.note: The Yuezhi who stayed in the Southern Mountains when the rest went west, living among the Qiang; under the Eastern Han they served as the Huangzhong auxiliaries.

items.note: 武都、阴平一带的部族，白马氐最大，武帝时置武都郡。

e.note: A people of Wudu and Yinping, the Baima Di the largest; Wudu Commandery was set up among them under Emperor Wu.

items.note: 阿尔金山一带随畜逐水草的羌人，不田作。

e.note: Qiang of the Altun Mountains who followed their herds and did not farm.

items.note: 青藏高原腹地的羌人部落，或以为吐蕃之先。

e.note: Qiang tribes deep in the Tibetan plateau, sometimes thought to be forerunners of the Tibetans.

items.note: 朝鲜半岛东部的部族，前128 年濊君南闾降汉。

e.note: A people of the eastern Korean peninsula; their chief Namnyeo submitted to Han in 128 BC.

items.note: 夫余以东的林中部族，善射，即古之肃慎，曾臣属夫余。

e.note: Forest dwellers east of Buyeo, skilled archers, identified with the ancient Sushen; once subject to Buyeo.

items.note: 日本列岛的倭人，《汉书》称「分为百余国」，57 年倭奴国奉贡。

e.note: The Wa of the Japanese islands, 'divided into more than a hundred states' according to the Han shu; the state of Na sent tribute in 57.

items.note: 江南山地的越人，东汉时屡起反抗。

e.note: The Yue of the hills of Jiangnan, who often rose against the Eastern Han.

items.note: 红河流域与岭南西部的越人。

e.note: The Yue of the Red River valley and western Lingnan.

items.note: 洱海一带随畜迁徙的部族，屡劫杀汉使，阻通身毒之道。

e.note: Herders around Lake Erhai who repeatedly attacked Han envoys and blocked the route to India.

items.note: 咸海以北的游牧之国（阿兰聊），控弦十余万。

e.note: A nomadic state north of the Aral Sea (Alanliao, i.e. the Alans), with over a hundred thousand archers.

items.note: 荥阳北广武山上，楚汉相持之地。东西两城隔广武涧对峙，相传西为汉王城、东为霸王城，今人也把这道涧叫作鸿沟。前203 年项羽置太公于俎上欲烹之，刘邦答以「幸分我一杯羹」；项羽请与汉王独身挑战，汉王数项羽十大罪，被伏弩射中胸口，扪足曰「虏中吾指」以安军心。

e.note: On Mount Guangwu north of Xingyang, where Chu and Han faced each other for months. Two forts stand on either side of the Guangwu ravine, by tradition the Han King's fort to the west and the Hegemon-King's to the east, and the ravine itself is nowadays also called the Honggou. In 203 BC Xiang Yu set Liu Bang's father on a chopping block and threatened to boil him; Liu Bang replied that he hoped to be sent a cup of the broth. When Xiang Yu challenged him to single combat, the king of Han listed Xiang Yu's ten great crimes and was hit in the chest by a hidden crossbowman; clutching his foot, he cried 'The wretch has hit my toe!' to keep his army steady.

items.mod: 河南灵宝北（秦函谷关遗址）
items.note: 战国时秦所置的东方门户，在今灵宝王垛村，扼崤函古道。前206 年刘邦先入关中，遣兵守函谷关；项羽至，不得入，使当阳君黥布等击破关城。前114 年关东移至新安（见新安的函谷关），故关改置弘农县。

e.mod: north of Lingbao, Henan (Qin Hangu Pass site)
e.note: Qin's eastern gateway, set up in the Warring States period at today's Wangduo village in Lingbao, commanding the road through the Xiao and Hangu defiles. In 206 BC Liu Bang, the first to enter Guanzhong, sent troops to hold the Hangu Pass; when Xiang Yu arrived and could not get through, he had Qing Bu, Lord of Dangyang, and others storm it. In 114 BC the pass was moved east to Xin'an (see the Hangu Pass at Xin'an), and the county of Hongnong was set up at the old pass.

items.note: 武关通关中的要隘，刘邦入关曾袭破之。

e.note: The key pass on the road from the Wu Pass into Guanzhong, taken by Liu Bang on his way in.

items.note: 黄河蒲津渡口西岸，关中东北门户。

e.note: The west bank of the Pujin ferry over the Yellow River, Guanzhong's north-eastern gate.

items.note: 阴山缺口，赵武灵王置塞，卫青由此出击。

e.mod: Langshan, western Yin Mountains, Inner Mongolia
e.note: A gap in the Yin Mountains fortified by King Wuling of Zhao; Wei Qing struck out from here.

items.note: 朔方郡西北塞口，在今磴口西北哈隆格乃峡谷口，存石筑障城。始筑年代史无明文，当在前127 年置朔方郡以后；前51 年汉以骑兵一万六千护送呼韩邪单于由此出塞，是其首见；89 年窦宪出征北匈奴也由此出塞。

e.note: A frontier gate in the north-west of Shuofang Commandery, at the mouth of the Halonggenai gorge north-west of today's Dengkou, where a stone-walled fort survives. The sources do not say when it was built, though it was presumably after Shuofang Commandery was set up in 127 BC; it first appears in 51 BC, when sixteen thousand Han horsemen escorted the chanyu Huhanye out through it, and in AD 89 Dou Xian marched out through it against the Northern Xiongnu.

items.note: 前102 年路博德筑，出土汉简数万枚。

e.note: Built by Lu Bode in 102 BC; tens of thousands of Han wooden slips have been found here.

items.note: 西域都护治所。前60 年郑吉为西域都护，「中西域而立莫府，治乌垒城」。王莽时西域叛离，13 年焉耆杀都护但钦；16 年都护李崇兵败，退保龟兹；23 年王莽死，李崇没于西域，西域遂绝。东汉 74 年复置都护，陈睦的治所史无明文；91 年班超为都护，居龟兹它乾城。

e.note: Seat of the Protector-General of the Western Regions. In 60 BC Zheng Ji became Protector-General and 'set up his headquarters in the middle of the Western Regions, governing from the city of Wulei'. Under Wang Mang the Western Regions broke away: in AD 13 Yanqi killed the Protector-General Dan Qin, and in 16 the Protector-General Li Chong was defeated and fell back to hold Qiuci; when Wang Mang died in 23 Li Chong was lost, and contact with the Western Regions ceased. When the Eastern Han restored the office in 74, the sources do not say where the new Protector-General, Chen Mu, had his seat; from 91 Ban Chao, as Protector-General, was based at Tagan in Qiuci.

items.note: 东汉戊己校尉、西域长史屯田之所。74 年复置戊己校尉，关宠屯柳中城；次年北匈奴与车师围攻，76 年汉军赶到时关宠已死，遂罢戊己校尉。123 年班勇为西域长史，将弛刑士五百人西屯柳中，次年起平定车师前后部。

e.note: Farming garrison of the Eastern Han Wu-Ji colonel and the Chief Clerk of the Western Regions. When the Wu-Ji colonels were restored in AD 74, Guan Chong was stationed at the town of Liuzhong; the next year the Northern Xiongnu and Jushi besieged him, and by the time a Han relief force arrived in 76 he was dead, and the office of Wu-Ji colonel was abolished. In 123 Ban Yong, as Chief Clerk of the Western Regions, led five hundred convict soldiers west to garrison Liuzhong, and from the next year subdued the Front and Rear kingdoms of Jushi.

items.mod: 蒙古国杭爱山南麓（一说；点位示意）
items.note: 前123 年赵信兵败复降匈奴，单于以为自次王，以姊妻之，筑城居之，故名。前119 年卫青追单于至窴颜山赵信城，取其积粟食军，留一日，悉烧余粟而还。史籍只说在窴颜山下，今地无定说：一说在杭爱山南麓（窴颜山为杭爱山南支），图上取此说；一说在色楞格河支流哈努伊河中游，附近有匈奴古城遗址；蒙古学者曾把南戈壁省巴彦布拉格城址比作赵信城，主持发掘的俄罗斯学者科瓦列夫则认为是汉受降城，城中合葬的士卒经古 DNA 与同位素分析为华北人。谭其骧《中国历史地图集》不标。

e.mod: southern foot of the Khangai Mountains, Mongolia (one view; approximate)
e.note: After his defeat in 123 BC Zhao Xin went back over to the Xiongnu; the chanyu made him the Zici king, gave him his elder sister in marriage and built a fort for him to live in, hence its name. In 119 BC Wei Qing pursued the chanyu to Zhao Xin's fort at Mount Tianyan, fed his army on the grain stored there, stayed one day and burned the rest. The sources say only that it lay below Mount Tianyan, and its modern site is unsettled: one view puts it at the southern foot of the Khangai Mountains (Mount Tianyan being a southern spur of the Khangai), which the map follows; another on the middle Khanuy River, a tributary of the Selenge, near the ruins of a Xiongnu walled town. Mongolian scholars once identified the walled site of Bayanbulag in Ömnögovi as Zhao Xin's fort, but its excavator, the Russian archaeologist Alexey Kovalev, takes it for the Han fort of Shouxiang, and ancient DNA and isotope analysis show that the soldiers buried together there came from northern China. Tan Qixiang's Historical Atlas of China does not mark it.

items.mod: 蒙古国南戈壁省瑙木冈苏木南（巴彦布拉格城址；一说内蒙古乌拉特中旗东）
items.note: 「受降」即接受投降。前105 年乌维单于死，子儿单于年少好杀，国人多不安，匈奴左大都尉暗中派人告汉：欲杀单于来降，汉远，请发兵来迎。前104 年武帝令因杅将军公孙敖出塞筑城以待，仍嫌太远。次年浞野侯赵破奴率二万骑出朔方西北二千余里接应，左大都尉事泄被杀，赵破奴回师途中在距受降城四百里处被八万骑围困，全军覆没；单于乘胜遣兵攻城，不能下。此后城孤悬塞外，汉匈反复争夺：前81 年壶衍鞮单于派九千骑屯驻于此以备汉；前71 年五将军出击时，城中设有汉朝的受降都尉；前51 年呼韩邪单于附汉，请居光禄塞下，「有急保汉受降城」。史书只说在塞外；2009 年俄蒙考古队认为即巴彦布拉格城址，城旁乱葬坑出土的士卒经基因与同位素分析来自华北，但最早的尸骨测年早于筑城，比定仍有争议。

e.mod: south of Nomgon sum, Ömnögovi, Mongolia (Bayanbulag site; another view: east of Urad Middle Banner, Inner Mongolia)
e.note: Shouxiang means 'receiving surrender'. In 105 BC the chanyu Wuwei died; his son, the boy chanyu, was young and fond of killing, and many of his people were uneasy. The Xiongnu Chief Commandant of the Left secretly sent word to Han that he meant to kill the chanyu and surrender, and asked for troops to meet him, since Han was far away. In 104 BC Emperor Wu had Gongsun Ao, the Yinyu General, build a fort beyond the frontier to receive him, though even that was thought too far. The next year Zhao Ponu, Marquis of Zhuoye, led twenty thousand horsemen more than two thousand li north-west from Shuofang to meet the commandant, but the plot was discovered and the commandant killed; on the way back Zhao Ponu was surrounded by eighty thousand horsemen four hundred li short of the fort and his whole army was lost. The chanyu then sent troops against the fort, but they could not take it. Standing alone beyond the frontier, it changed hands more than once: in 81 BC the chanyu Huyandi stationed nine thousand horsemen here against Han, when five Han generals took the field against the Xiongnu in 71 BC, a Han Commandant for Receiving Surrender was stationed there; and in 51 BC Huhanye, newly submitted to Han, asked to stay by the Guanglu frontier and, 'in an emergency, to take refuge in the Han fort of Shouxiang'. The sources say only that it lay beyond the frontier. In 2009 a Russian–Mongolian team identified it with the walled site of Bayanbulag. DNA and isotope analysis shows that the soldiers in a mass grave beside it came from northern China, but the earliest skeletons date from before the fort was built, so the identification is still debated.

items.note: 前121 年浑邪王降汉、河西归汉，前119 年以后汉「渡河自朔方以西至令居，往往通渠置田」；约前115 年张骞自乌孙归后，「汉始筑令居以西」，是为河西塞的起点。

e.note: After the Hunye king surrendered in 121 BC and the Hexi Corridor passed to Han, from 119 BC Han 'crossed the [Yellow] River and, from Shuofang west to Lingju, dug canals and set up farms in many places'; around 115 BC, after Zhang Qian came back from the Wusun, 'Han began to build [fortifications] west of Lingju', making Lingju the starting point of the Hexi frontier.

items.mod: 甘肃兰州—宁夏—内蒙古河套、阴山
items.note: 蒙恬取河南地后，“因河为塞”，沿黄河设亭障，又越河筑城于阴山、高阙一带，与秦昭王、赵、燕旧长城连成“万里长城”，西起临洮，东至辽东。

e.mod: Lanzhou, Gansu – Ningxia – Hetao and Yin Mountains, Inner Mongolia
e.note: After taking Henandi, Meng Tian "used the river as a barrier", setting up watchtowers and stockades along the Yellow River; he also crossed the river and built walls and forts around the Yin Mountains and Gaoque, joining them with the old long walls of King Zhao of Qin, Zhao and Yan into the "Great Wall", from Lintao in the west to Liaodong in the east.

items.mod: 甘肃临洮—宁夏固原—陕西榆林
items.note: 灭义渠后所筑，西起临洮，经固原、环县、吴起、靖边至榆林、神木，拒北方胡人。秦统一后成为万里长城西段。

e.old: Long Wall of King Zhao of Qin
e.mod: Lintao, Gansu – Guyuan, Ningxia – Yulin, Shaanxi
e.note: Built after the destruction of Yiqu, from Lintao in the west through Guyuan, Huan County, Wuqi and Jingbian to Yulin and Shenmu, against the northern Hu. After the Qin unification it became the western section of the Great Wall.

items.mod: 河北张家口—内蒙古阴山—高阙
items.note: 赵武灵王破林胡、楼烦后，“筑长城，自代并阴山下，至高阙为塞”。秦统一后为万里长城所沿用。

e.mod: Zhangjiakou, Hebei – Yin Mountains, Inner Mongolia – Gaoque
e.note: After crushing the Linhu and Loufan, King Wuling of Zhao "built a long wall from Dai along the foot of the Yin Mountains to Gaoque as a barrier". After the Qin unification it was taken into the Great Wall.

items.mod: 河北张家口—内蒙古赤峰—辽宁辽阳
items.note: 秦开却东胡后，燕“筑长城，自造阳至襄平”，置五郡以拒胡。秦统一后为万里长城东段。

e.mod: Zhangjiakou, Hebei – Chifeng, Inner Mongolia – Liaoyang, Liaoning
e.note: After Qin Kai drove back the Donghu, Yan "built a long wall from Zaoyang to Xiangping" and set up five commanderies against the Hu. After the Qin unification it became the eastern section of the Great Wall.

items.note: 以咸阳为中心修筑的全国干道，“东穷燕齐，南极吴楚”，道宽五十步，三丈而树（《汉书·贾山传》）。走向为示意。

e.note: The trunk roads of the realm, built with Xianyang at their centre, "reaching Yan and Qi in the east and Wu and Chu in the south", fifty paces wide and planted with a tree every three zhang (Hanshu, biography of Jia Shan). The routes are schematic.

items.note: 蒙恬主持修筑，自云阳（甘泉宫）沿子午岭北上直抵九原，“堑山堙谷，千八百里”，三日之内骑兵可自咸阳抵达阴山（据今人推算）。

e.note: Built under Meng Tian, running north from Yunyang (the Ganquan Palace) along the Ziwu Ridge straight to Jiuyuan, "cutting through hills and filling valleys for eighteen hundred li"; cavalry could ride from Xianyang to the Yin Mountains within three days (a modern estimate).

items.note: 常頞开凿，自僰道（今宜宾）南下通往夜郎、滇池，因山路险窄，宽仅五尺。

e.note: Cut by Chang E, running south from Bodao (modern Yibin) to Yelang and Lake Dian; because the mountain road was steep and narrow it was only five feet wide.

items.note: 前121 年后自令居西筑塞，前111—前101 年延至酒泉、玉门、盐泽，烽燧相望。

e.mod: Yongdeng to west of Dunhuang, Gansu
e.note: After 121 BC a frontier was built west from Lingju, extended in 111–101 BC to Jiuquan, the Jade Gate and the Salt Marsh, with beacon towers in sight of one another.

items.mod: 甘肃金塔—内蒙古额济纳
items.note: 前102 年路博德筑，沿弱水北至居延泽，遮断匈奴南下河西之路。

e.mod: Jinta, Gansu to Ejin, Inner Mongolia
e.note: Built by Lu Bode in 102 BC along the Ruo River north to Lake Juyan, blocking the Xiongnu route south into Hexi.

items.note: 前102 年光禄勋徐自为筑五原塞外列城，远者千余里，史称光禄塞。

e.mod: north of the Yin Mountains, Inner Mongolia
e.note: Built in 102 BC by Xu Ziwei, Superintendent of the Palace, as a chain of forts beyond the Wuyuan frontier, the farthest more than a thousand li out: the Guanglu frontier.

items.note: 戍卒九百人屯大泽乡，遇雨失期，陈胜、吴广杀将尉起事，攻蕲，分兵东略，主力西攻铚、酂、谯、苦等县，行收兵，至陈已有车六七百乘、骑千余、卒数万。

e.old: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang's rising
e.note: Nine hundred conscripts held up by rain at Dazexiang killed their officers and rose under Chen Sheng and Wu Guang. They took Qi, sent a detachment east, and with the main force struck west, taking Zhi, Cuo, Qiao, Ku and other counties, gathering men as they went; by the time they reached Chen they had six or seven hundred chariots, over a thousand horsemen and tens of thousands of foot.

items.note: 陈胜遣周文西击秦，沿途收兵，入函谷关时有车千乘、卒数十万，九月至戏。章邯发骊山刑徒击破之，周文退出关，止曹阳，再败于渑池，自刎。

e.note: Chen Sheng sent Zhou Wen west against Qin. Gathering men along the way, he passed the Hangu Pass with a thousand chariots and several hundred thousand men and reached Xi in the 9th month. Zhang Han, arming the Lishan labourers, routed him; Zhou Wen fell back through the pass to Caoyang, was beaten again at Mianchi and cut his own throat.

items.note: 楚怀王遣沛公西略地入关。沛公自砀北破东郡尉于成武，攻昌邑不下，西袭陈留，攻开封，破秦将杨熊于曲遇，南屠颍阳；入南阳，降宛，破武关，用张良计袭破峣关下秦军于蓝田，汉元年十月至霸上，子婴出降。

e.note: King Huai of Chu sent the Lord of Pei west to win land and enter the passes. From Dang he struck north and beat the commandant of Dong Commandery at Chengwu, failed to take Changyi, fell on Chenliu, attacked Kaifeng, beat the Qin general Yang Xiong at Quyu and sacked Yingyang to the south. He then entered Nanyang, took the surrender of Wan, broke through the Wu Pass and, on Zhang Liang's advice, routed the Qin army below the Yao Pass at Lantian; in the 10th month of Han year 1 he reached Bashang, where Ziying surrendered.

items.note: 宋义、项羽北救赵，宋义留安阳四十六日不进，项羽杀之，引兵渡河，破釜沉舟，大破秦军于巨鹿；章邯降于殷墟。项羽率诸侯兵西进，坑秦降卒二十余万于新安，破函谷关，军鸿门，引兵屠咸阳。

e.old: Xiang Yu relieves Zhao and enters Guanzhong
e.note: Song Yi and Xiang Yu marched north to relieve Zhao. When Song Yi waited forty-six days at Anyang without advancing, Xiang Yu killed him, crossed the Yellow River, sank his boats, broke his pots and routed the Qin army at Julu; Zhang Han surrendered at the ruins of Yin. Leading the allied armies west, Xiang Yu buried over 200,000 surrendered Qin soldiers alive at Xin'an, forced the Hangu Pass, camped at Hongmen and then sacked Xianyang.

items.note: 汉王用韩信计，自南郑出故道，袭雍王章邯于陈仓，围废丘，东至咸阳、栎阳，塞王司马欣、翟王董翳皆降。

e.note: On Han Xin's plan the king of Han came out of Nanzheng by the Old Road, fell on Zhang Han, king of Yong, at Chencang and besieged Feiqiu, then moved east to Xianyang and Yueyang; Sima Xin, king of Sai, and Dong Yi, king of Di, both surrendered.

items.note: 汉王自临晋渡河，下河内，至洛阳为义帝发丧，率五诸侯兵五十六万东伐楚，四月入彭城，收其货宝美人，日置酒高会。

e.note: The king of Han crossed the Yellow River at Linjin, took Henei and, at Luoyang, proclaimed mourning for the Righteous Emperor; leading 560,000 men of five allied lords east against Chu, he entered Pengcheng in the 4th month, seized its treasure and women, and feasted day after day.

items.note: 项羽闻汉入彭城，留诸将击齐，自以精兵三万人南从鲁出胡陵，晨击汉军于萧，东至彭城，日中大破汉军；汉卒十余万人入睢水，水为之不流。

e.note: Hearing that Han had entered Pengcheng, Xiang Yu left his generals to fight Qi and took 30,000 picked men south through Lu and out by Huling. He struck the Han army at Xiao at dawn, pressed east to Pengcheng and by midday had routed it; more than a hundred thousand Han soldiers were driven into the Sui River until it stopped flowing.

items.note: 韩信自临晋声言渡河，伏兵从夏阳以木罂渡军，袭安邑，虏魏豹；后九月破代于阏与；次年十月东下井陉，背水一战破赵；又东击齐，袭破历下，入临淄，十一月破龙且于潍水。

e.note: Han Xin feinted a crossing at Linjin while his men crossed upstream at Xiayang on wooden jars, fell on Anyi and captured Wei Bao; in the intercalary 9th month he broke Dai at Yuyu; in the 10th month of the next year he came down Jingxing and, fighting with his back to the river, destroyed Zhao. He then struck east into Qi, overran Lixia, entered Linzi and in the 11th month beat Long Ju on the Wei River.

items.note: 元光六年，匈奴入上谷杀略吏民，汉遣四将军各将万骑出击：卫青以车骑将军出上谷，至龙城，斩首虏七百；公孙敖出代、李广出雁门皆败，公孙贺出云中无功。

e.note: In Yuanguang 6, after the Xiongnu had raided Shanggu, killing and carrying off officials and people, Han sent four generals with ten thousand horsemen each against them. Wei Qing, as General of Chariots and Cavalry, went out from Shanggu to Longcheng and took seven hundred heads and prisoners; Gongsun Ao from Dai and Li Guang from Yanmen were both defeated, and Gongsun He from Yunzhong achieved nothing.

items.note: 卫青出云中，沿河西行至高阙，南下至陇西，包抄河南匈奴，走白羊、楼烦王，遂取河南地，置朔方、五原郡。

e.note: Wei Qing set out from Yunzhong, followed the river west to Gaoque and swept south to Longxi, enveloping the Xiongnu of the Ordos; he drove off the Baiyang and Loufan kings, took the Ordos and set up Shuofang and Wuyuan commanderies.

items.note: 元朔五年春，卫青将三万骑出朔方高阙，诸将合十余万分道并出；北行六七百里，夜至右贤王庭围之，右贤王溃围北走，汉军俘裨王十余人、众万五千余口而还，卫青就军中拜大将军。

e.old: Wei Qing's night raid on the Wise King of the Right
e.note: In the spring of Yuanshuo 5 Wei Qing led 30,000 horsemen out from Gaoque in Shuofang, while the other generals, bringing the total to more than 100,000 men, advanced by separate roads. Six or seven hundred li to the north he reached the camp of the Wise King of the Right by night and surrounded it; the king broke out and fled north, and the Han army came back with more than ten lesser kings and over 15,000 captives. Wei Qing was made Grand General in the field.

items.note: 元朔六年二月，大将军卫青率中、左、前、右、后、强弩六将军十余万骑出定襄，斩首三千余级，还师休士马于定襄、云中、雁门；四月复出定襄，斩首虏万余。前将军赵信、右将军苏建并军三千余骑独遇单于，战一日余，汉兵且尽，赵信降匈奴，苏建独身脱还。

e.old: Wei Qing's two sorties from Dingxiang
e.note: In the 2nd month of Yuanshuo 6 the Grand General Wei Qing led six generals and more than 100,000 horsemen out of Dingxiang, took over 3,000 heads and fell back to rest his men and horses in Dingxiang, Yunzhong and Yanmen; in the 4th month he went out from Dingxiang again and took over 10,000 heads and prisoners. The General of the Van, Zhao Xin, and the General of the Right, Su Jian, whose combined force of more than 3,000 horsemen ran into the chanyu on their own, fought for more than a day until their men were nearly all gone; Zhao Xin went over to the Xiongnu and Su Jian escaped alone.

items.note: 同年四月，年十八的剽姚校尉霍去病与轻勇骑八百，弃大军数百里赴利，斩首虏二千零二十八级，斩单于大父行籍若侯产，生捕季父罗姑比，功冠全军，封冠军侯。

e.note: In the 4th month of the same year Huo Qubing, the eighteen-year-old Piaoyao Colonel, rode with eight hundred light horse several hundred li ahead of the main army, took 2,028 heads and prisoners, killed Chan, Marquis of Jiruo, a member of the chanyu's grandfather's generation, and captured the chanyu's uncle Luogubi; his feat outshone the whole army, and he was made Marquis of Guanjun.

items.note: 元狩二年春，霍去病将万骑出陇西，转战六日，过焉支山千余里，杀折兰王、卢胡王，获休屠王祭天金人。

e.note: In the spring of 121 BC Huo Qubing led ten thousand horsemen out of Longxi, fought for six days and pushed over a thousand li past Mount Yanzhi, killing the Zhelan and Luhu kings and taking the golden statue the Xiutu king used to worship Heaven.

items.note: 同年夏，霍去病出北地，逾居延泽，南下经小月氏，攻祁连山，得酋涂王，斩首虏三万二百级，获五王、五王母、单于阏氏、王子五十九人，相国、将军、当户、都尉六十三人；秋，浑邪王杀休屠王，率四万余人降汉，河西归汉。

e.note: That summer Huo Qubing set out from Beidi, passed Lake Juyan, turned south through the Lesser Yuezhi lands and struck at the Qilian Mountains, where he took the Qiutu king and 30,200 heads and prisoners, capturing five kings and five kings' mothers, the chanyu's consort, fifty-nine princes and sixty-three chancellors, generals, danghu and commandants. In the autumn the Hunye king killed the Xiutu king and surrendered with over 40,000 people, and Hexi passed to Han.

items.note: 卫青出定襄，北行千余里，遇伊稚斜单于陈兵以待，以武刚车环为营，纵五千骑往击；日暮大风扬沙，汉益纵左右翼绕单于，单于溃围西北走。卫青追二百余里不及，至窴颜山赵信城，取其积粟食军，留一日，悉烧余粟而还。前将军李广、右将军赵食其并军出东道，惑失道，后大将军，李广引刀自刭。

e.note: Wei Qing set out from Dingxiang and marched over a thousand li north, where the chanyu Yizhixie was drawn up waiting. Circling his armoured wagons into a laager, he loosed five thousand horse at him; at dusk a gale threw up the sand, Han sent its wings round the chanyu, and he broke out to the north-west. Wei Qing pursued for over two hundred li without catching him, reached Zhao Xin's fort at Mount Tianyan, fed his army on the grain stored there, stayed one day, burned the rest and turned back. Li Guang, General of the Van, and Zhao Shiqi, General of the Right, sent together by the eastern road, lost their way and arrived after the battle; Li Guang cut his own throat.

items.note: 霍去病出代二千余里，绝大幕，历涉离侯，济弓闾，破左贤王，斩首虏七万余，获屯头王、韩王等三人及将军、相国、当户、都尉八十三人，封狼居胥山，禅于姑衍，登临翰海而还。弓闾一般认为即弓卢水（克鲁伦河）；翰海所指诸说不一，这里取贝加尔湖说。

e.note: Huo Qubing marched more than two thousand li from Dai, crossed the great desert, passed Lihou and crossed the Gonglü, broke the Wise King of the Left and took over 70,000 heads and prisoners, capturing three kings, among them the Xiongnu kings of Tuntou and Han, and eighty-three generals, chancellors, danghu and commandants; he sacrificed to Heaven on Mount Langjuxu and to Earth on Mount Guyan, climbed to look out over the Hanhai and turned back. The Gonglü is usually taken to be the Gonglu River (Kherlen); views differ on what the Hanhai was, and the map follows the Lake Baikal identification.

items.note: 张骞出陇西，过河西为匈奴所得，留十余年；乘间西走，经大宛、康居至大月氏，又至大夏，留岁余。

e.note: Zhang Qian went out through Longxi and was caught by the Xiongnu as he crossed Hexi; they held him for over ten years. He slipped away west through Dayuan and Kangju to the Great Yuezhi and on to Daxia, where he stayed a year and more.

items.note: 张骞并南山，欲从羌中归，复为匈奴所得，留岁余；军臣单于死，匈奴国内乱，张骞乘机逃归长安。

e.note: Zhang Qian went home along the Southern Mountains, meaning to pass through the Qiang lands, but was caught again by the Xiongnu and held for over a year; when the chanyu Junchen died and the Xiongnu fell into turmoil he escaped to Chang'an.

items.note: 南越相吕嘉反，杀其王及汉使。伏波将军路博德出桂阳，下湟水，与杨仆会师，俱进番禺，元鼎六年冬破番禺，南越亡。

e.note: When Lü Jia, chancellor of Nanyue, rebelled and killed his king and the Han envoys, Lu Bode, General Who Calms the Waves, set out from Guiyang, went down the Huang River and joined Yang Pu, advancing with him on Panyu; Panyu fell in the winter of 111 BC and Nanyue fell with it.

items.note: 楼船将军杨仆出豫章，越横浦关，下浈水，先陷寻陕、石门，率精卒先至番禺，纵火烧城。

e.note: Yang Pu, General of the Towered Ships, set out from Yuzhang, crossed the Hengpu Pass and went down the Zhen River, took Xunxia and Shimen first and reached Panyu ahead of the others with his picked troops, setting the city on fire.

items.note: 元封二年秋，楼船将军杨仆自齐浮渤海，率齐兵七千先至王险城下，为朝鲜所败，收散卒；次年与左将军荀彘合围，夏，朝鲜相杀其王右渠来降。

e.note: In the autumn of 109 BC Yang Pu, General of the Towered Ships, sailed from Qi across the Bohai and reached Wangxian first with seven thousand men of Qi, but was beaten and had to regather his scattered men; the next year he and Xun Zhi, General of the Left, besieged the city together, and in the summer Joseon ministers killed their king Ugeo and surrendered.

items.note: 左将军荀彘将燕、代卒出辽东，初击浿水西军不能破，后破浿水上军，进至王险城下，围其西北。

e.note: Xun Zhi, General of the Left, led troops of Yan and Dai out of Liaodong; he failed at first against the Joseon army west of the Pae River, then broke the force on the river, reached Wangxian and besieged it from the north-west.

items.note: 贰师将军李广利再伐大宛，率六万人出敦煌，过盐泽，屠轮台，西越葱岭北麓，围贵山城四十余日，宛贵人杀其王毋寡请降，汉立昧蔡为王；别将上官桀攻破郁成。

e.note: On his second campaign against Dayuan, the Ershi General Li Guangli led 60,000 men out of Dunhuang past the Salt Marsh, sacked Luntai, crossed the northern flank of the Pamirs and besieged Guishan for over forty days, until the nobles of Dayuan killed their king Wugua and surrendered; Han installed Meicai as king. A detachment under Shangguan Jie took Yucheng.

items.note: 西域副校尉陈汤矫诏发西域诸国兵与屯田吏士四万余人，与都护甘延寿分两道：三校从南道越葱岭、经大宛，三校从北道入赤谷、过乌孙，会于康居，围郅支城，斩郅支单于。

e.note: Chen Tang, Deputy Colonel of the Western Regions, forged an edict to raise over 40,000 men from the oasis states and the garrison farms, and with the Protector-General Gan Yanshou marched in two columns — three regiments over the Pamirs by the southern road through Dayuan, three by the northern road through Chigu and Wusun — to meet in Kangju, besiege Zhizhi's fortress and behead the chanyu.

items.note: 更始元年十月，刘秀以破虏将军行大司马事持节北渡河，镇慰河北州郡，至邯郸、真定，北上蓟；王郎在邯郸称帝，悬赏购之，刘秀自蓟南逃，经饶阳、下曲阳渡滹沱河，至信都，收兵反攻，次年五月破邯郸、诛王郎。建武元年六月即位于鄗，十月入洛阳。

e.note: In the 10th month of AD 23 Liu Xiu crossed the Yellow River as acting Grand Marshal with the Gengshi emperor's tally to win over the commanderies of Hebei, passing through Handan and Zhending and north to Ji. When Wang Lang proclaimed himself emperor at Handan and put a price on his head, Liu Xiu fled south from Ji through Raoyang and Xiaquyang, crossed the Hutuo River and reached Xindu, where he raised troops and struck back, taking Handan and killing Wang Lang in the 5th month of 24. He took the throne at Hao in the 6th month of 25 and entered Luoyang in the 10th.

items.note: 建武十一年，岑彭率舟师攻破荆门、虎牙，溯江入江关，至江州，倍道兼行二千余里至武阳，为公孙述所遣刺客所杀；次年吴汉继进，破广都，围成都，十一月公孙述伤重而死，蜀平。

e.old: Cen Peng and Wu Han against Shu
e.note: In AD 35 Cen Peng's fleet broke the barrier at Jingmen and Huya, sailed up the Yangzi through the Jiang Pass to Jiangzhou and drove on over two thousand li to Wuyang, where he was murdered by an assassin sent by Gongsun Shu; the next year Wu Han pressed on, took Guangdu and besieged Chengdu, and in the 11th month Gongsun Shu died of his wounds and Shu was won.

items.note: 征侧、征贰起兵，岭南六十余城响应。伏波将军马援自合浦缘海而进，随山刊道千余里，破征侧于浪泊，次年斩之，进击九真余部至居风。

e.note: When the Trưng sisters rose and more than sixty towns south of the Five Ranges joined them, Ma Yuan, General Who Calms the Waves, advanced from Hepu along the coast, cutting a road through the hills for over a thousand li, beat Trưng Trắc at Langbo, beheaded her the next year and pursued the remnants in Jiuzhen as far as Jufeng.

items.note: 永平十六年班超以假司马随窦固击伊吾，旋率吏士三十六人出使：在鄯善夜袭匈奴使者，鄯善降；至于阗，斩巫，于阗王广德杀匈奴使者而降；明年春至疏勒，执龟兹所立的疏勒王兜题。76 年都护罢后，超还疏勒坚守，78 年率疏勒、康居、于阗、拘弥兵一万攻破姑墨石城，87 年发于阗诸国兵二万五千破莎车，91 年为都护，居龟兹它乾城，94 年发八国兵七万讨平焉耆。超在西域三十一年，102 年东归，同年卒。

e.old: Ban Chao in the Western Regions
e.note: In Yongping 16 Ban Chao, an acting major, fought under Dou Gu at Yiwu and was then sent west with thirty-six men. At Shanshan he fell on the Xiongnu envoys by night and Shanshan submitted; at Khotan he beheaded a shaman, and King Guangde killed the Xiongnu envoys and submitted; the next spring he reached Kashgar and seized Douti, the king Kucha had imposed there. After the Protectorate was abandoned in 76 he went back to hold Kashgar; in 78 he led 10,000 men from Kashgar, Kangju, Khotan and Jumi to storm the stone fort of Gumo, in 87 he took Yarkand with 25,000 men from Khotan and its neighbours, in 91 he became Protector-General at Tuoqian in Kucha, and in 94 he crushed Karasahr with 70,000 men from eight states. He spent thirty-one years in the Western Regions and went home in 102, dying the same year.

items.note: 建初元年正月，援军破车师于交河城，军吏范羌领兵二千越天山，雪深丈余，至疏勒城迎耿恭。耿恭余众随之东归，虏兵追之，且战且行，发疏勒时尚有二十六人，随路死没，三月至玉门，唯余十三人，衣屦穿决，形容枯槁。

e.old: Geng Gong's return to the Jade Gate
e.note: In the 1st month of Jianchu 1, after the relief army had broken Jushi at Jiaohe, the officer Fan Qiang took 2,000 men over the Tianshan through snow more than a zhang deep to bring out Geng Gong from the fort of Shule. Geng Gong and his remaining men went east with Fan Qiang, fighting off the pursuing enemy as they marched; twenty-six of them left Shule, men died along the way, and when they reached the Jade Gate in the 3rd month only thirteen were left, their clothes and shoes in tatters and their faces gaunt.

items.note: 车骑将军窦宪与南单于等分三道出塞，自出鸡鹿塞，会诸军于涿邪山，大破北单于于稽落山，追至私渠比鞮海，登燕然山，令班固作铭，刻石记功而还。

e.note: Dou Xian, General of Chariots and Cavalry, went out beyond the frontier in three columns with the southern chanyu; he set out himself from the Jilu frontier post, joined the other columns at Mount Zhuoye, crushed the northern chanyu at Mount Jiluo, pursued him to Lake Siqubiti, then climbed Mount Yanran, had Ban Gu compose an inscription and carved it in the rock before turning back.
